title: [bug] clip-win-bridge.sh never starts from i3: powershell.exe is not on i3's PATH, so the guard exits 0 silently
notes:
ROOT CAUSE
  PS=powershell.exe; command -v "$PS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
powershell.exe on this host is a symlink in ~/.local/bin/win/, which the login
profile adds to PATH but i3 does NOT — i3's PATH (read from /proc/888/environ)
is /home/jan/.local/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin:... So the wsl.conf
autostart resolved nothing and took the silent success branch: the Windows<->X
clipboard bridge NEVER ran from i3.

Every clip-win-bridge.sh process found alive on this box was a ppid=1 leftover
from agent session f8dc51f8, started from an interactive shell. That is the
mechanism behind the recurring 'clipboard from Windows is broken again':
after any reboot or i3 restart there was no bridge, and it 'fixed itself'
whenever someone started it by hand.

Found by killing those leftovers (user request) and watching i3's restart
bring back clip-store and clip-img-bridge but not this one.

FIX  resolve PATH -> $HOME/.local/bin/win/powershell.exe -> $WSL_MARK/Windows/
System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe, and split the gate: not WSL
-> exit 0 silent (native i3 autostarts this too); WSL but no interop -> exit
69 EX_UNAVAILABLE with a message, because a silent 0 reads as 'started fine'
in every ps/pgrep check.

TEST  i3/scripts/test-clip-win-bridge.sh, 6 asserts, no X/WSL/powershell
needed (stubs + an overridable CLIP_BRIDGE_WSL_MARK). RED 3/6 — exactly the
three assertions describing the bug; the two already-correct behaviours passed
before the fix, so the suite is not rubber-stamping.

VERIFIED LIVE  killed the hand-started bridge, ran i3 restart: bridge came
back at pid 2213605 with ppid=888 (i3-owned, first time ever). Win->X
'I3-OWNED-BRIDGE-5540' arrived in X; X->Win 'X-TO-WIN-8877' arrived in the
Windows clipboard. All four clip daemons now ppid=888, no agent stamps.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] hotkeyd's qs-overlay.sh dispatch cannot find the RDP session's embedded overlay — $mod+Tab / $mod+w open nothing on :10
description:
REPRODUCED LIVE on :10, 2026-07-29:

    $ DISPLAY=:10 qs-overlay.sh switcher
    qs-overlay: no quickshell instance for DISPLAY=:10

qs-overlay.sh's qs_target_pid() branches on the QS_RDP ENV VAR:
  QS_RDP=1 -> the overlay is embedded in the MAIN instance (no -p in cmdline)
  else     -> a separate `quickshell -p .../overlay` process
The :10 hotkeyd daemon's environ has DISPLAY=:10 and NO QS_RDP (checked
/proc/<pid>/environ). i3/config-xrdp sets QS_RDP only as the $qsenv PREFIX on
its own bindsym lines, and hotkeyd is not started from one of those. So every
overlay verb the DAEMON dispatches takes the desktop branch, looks for a
process that an RDP session deliberately does not run (qs-start.sh:133-136
skips it when QS_RDP=1), and exits 1.

WHY IT LOOKED FINE UNTIL NOW: the :10 session still had a stale separate
`-p overlay` instance from an earlier boot, so the desktop branch found
something. Restarting the session through qs-start.sh normalised it to the RDP
shape and the hole opened. The alt-tab cutover (dotfiles-hwds.40) moved the
switcher onto the daemon and inherited this dependency without noticing.

BLAST RADIUS: every daemon-dispatched overlay verb on an RDP session --
$mod+Tab, $mod+w (switcher), $mod+d (launcher), $mod+p (projects). $mod+n and
$mod+v are UNAFFECTED: qs-clip.sh / qs-notif.sh resolve the instance by
scanning for the session's quickshell rather than by trusting an env var, which
is the shape qs-overlay.sh should have.

FIX: make qs_target_pid DISCOVER instead of being told -- among this session's
quickshell pids, prefer one whose cmdline carries `-p <overlay>`, else fall
back to the main instance. Correct on both session types and independent of who
spawned the caller. Keep QS_RDP as an override if useful, but never as the sole
signal.

TEST: quickshell/test-overlay.sh already stands up a real instance; add a case
that resolves the target with QS_RDP UNSET against an RDP-shaped session (main
instance only) and asserts the verb reaches it.
close_reason:
FIXED, commit 13d6cc7. Self-verified.

qs_target_pid now DISCOVERS the host (prefer '-p <overlay>', else the session's
main instance) instead of branching on QS_RDP, which the daemon's environ never
carried. New suite quickshell/test-overlay-target.sh 6/0, all cases with QS_RDP
unset; mutation -- restoring the env-var branch turns 3 of 6 red. Regression:
test-overlay.sh 29/0, test-launcher.sh 27/0. LIVE on :10: $mod+w opens the
switcher and commits on release.

NOTE for whoever reads this later: the failure was INVISIBLE until the session
was restarted through qs-start.sh, because a stale separate overlay instance
from an earlier boot kept satisfying the desktop branch.

title: [bug] hotkeyd grab set is MONOTONIC across MappingNotify — an xrdp reconnect silently kills chords until restart, status says running
design:
USER-REPORTED, 2026-07-29, live :10 xrdp session. First as "nav mods not
working", then narrowed by the user to "direct $mod+hjkl not working, $mod+o is
correct". Both reports are the SAME defect.

=== WHAT WAS MEASURED ===

Live :10, daemon pid 3423823 (started 00:22, i.e. AFTER every cutover commit,
so its table was current -- 59 global chords, matching binds.py):

  xdotool alt+o    -> transition logged, layer=default->nav        WORKED
  xdotool alt+1    -> workspace switch fired (late, nushell start) WORKED
  xdotool alt+h/j/k/l/Left/Right/shift+h  -> nothing, 8 injections DEAD
  no BadAccess, no "i3 dispatch failed", no problem line in the log
  hotkeyd.sh status -> "running on :10"

After `hotkeyd.sh restart` on the SAME display, SAME workspace, SAME layout:

  alt+h  MOVED    alt+l  MOVED    alt+Left  MOVED    alt+Right  MOVED
  alt+z  fullscreen toggled and restored

So a subset of chords was silently unserved by a daemon reporting healthy, and
a restart was sufficient to restore them.

TWO ARTIFACTS RULED OUT, both of which faked a "DEAD" reading mid-session:
  - an injected $mod+1 landed workspace `morning-challenge` (ONE window), where
    focus left/right/up/down are legitimate no-ops. Every reading taken there is
    void; the pre-restart DEAD readings above were all taken on the 8-window
    `dotfiles` workspace, before any workspace drift.
  - alt+j / alt+k read DEAD even post-fix: that workspace is a tabbed container
    with no vertical neighbour, and bare `i3-msg focus down` no-ops identically.
    Layout, not daemon.
Also ruled out: cross-display dispatch (neither i3 moved), wrong IPC socket
(resolves to ipc-socket.2147 = the :10 i3), a stale table (59 chords = current),
i3 owning the chord (config.common no longer binds them, no panic latch in
~/.i3/config.d), and the engine itself (LayerEngine(mod='Mod1') returns
['focus left'] for a synthetic Mod1+h press).

=== ROOT CAUSE: GrabManager.on_mapping_notify (hotkeyd.py:476) ===

    r = self._resolve(chord)
    if r is None:
        self._ungrab(code, mask)
        del self._active[chord]     # <-- never re-added, by any path
        changed = True
        continue

1. THE RE-GRAB IS MONOTONIC. It iterates `self._active` -- what is STILL
   grabbed -- never the wanted chord list. The grab set can therefore only ever
   shrink. Nothing in the daemon re-derives it from the table after startup or
   a layer transition, so a chord dropped on one keymap churn is gone for the
   process lifetime.

2. THE LOSS IS SILENT. `self.problems` is cleared at line 481 (and again in
   sync_binds:449) and is printed ONLY at startup (hotkeyd.py:1185). Every
   mid-session grab failure is discarded unread. That is why the log showed
   "59 chords grabbed", zero BadAccess, and no problem line while the chords
   were already gone.

3. A REFUSED RE-GRAB IS ALSO A SILENT DROP. _grab (line 433) appends to
   problems and RETURNS before `self._active[chord] = (code, mask)`, so the
   chord is neither grabbed nor tracked -- and on_mapping_notify's `_grab` call
   at line 492 is exactly that path.

WHY XRDP TRIGGERS IT AND :0 LARGELY DOES NOT: xrdp reprograms the keymap on
every RDP (re)connect, so :10 gets MappingNotify churn that a native session
never sees. During the transient window while the keymap is being rebuilt,
keysym_to_keycode() can return 0 for keysyms that are about to exist again ->
_resolve returns None -> the chord is deleted permanently. Which chords die
depends on WHEN the notify lands, which is why the loss looks arbitrary
($mod+o survived, $mod+h did not) and why it is not reproducible on demand.

Related but distinct: dotfiles-hwds.28 (daemon survives its X server's death,
status lies) and dotfiles-hwds.29 (status cannot distinguish absent heartbeat
from stale) are the same family -- status proves LIVENESS, never SERVING. This
one needs the third thing: the grab set matching the table.

=== FIX DIRECTION ===
- on_mapping_notify must RE-SYNC AGAINST THE WANTED SET (the same chord list
  chords_for(table, current_layer) produces), not iterate the survivors. A
  keysym that is momentarily unresolvable must be retried when the keymap
  settles, not deleted.
- problems must be reported whenever they are produced, not only at startup.
  Every re-sync that ends with a non-empty problems list is a log line.
- hotkeyd.sh status should be able to answer "is the grab set the one the table
  asks for" -- a serving check, not a liveness check. Cheapest form: the daemon
  publishes grabbed-count + expected-count and status compares.

=== REGRESSION TEST (headless, no live :10 needed) ===
Drive GrabManager against a fake X whose keysym_to_keycode transiently returns
0 for one keysym, fire on_mapping_notify, let the keymap settle, fire again:
the chord MUST be grabbed again. Mutation check: today's code leaves it absent
and prints nothing.
close_reason:
FIXED in e0df62a2. on_mapping_notify and sync_binds now share one _apply() that
re-resolves the WANTED chord list (stored on sync_binds) instead of iterating
the survivors, so a chord lost to a transient keymap or refused at startup is
recovered on the next notify rather than stranded for the process lifetime.
Problems are reported when they occur, edge-triggered on message text so a
MappingNotify burst does not reprint.

EVIDENCE: 4 new tests in test_daemon.py, each mutation-verified (all 4 fail on
the pre-fix tree, all 4 pass after). pytest 341/0, test-hotkeyd.sh 107/0,
test-panic.sh 54/0, test-nav-mode.sh 40/0 both mod shapes. Live on :10 after
restarting the daemon on the fixed code: alt+h / alt+l / alt+Right all move
focus again.

FOLLOW-UP FILED SEPARATELY: hotkeyd.sh status still reports LIVENESS only -- it
said "running" through the entire outage. A serving check (grabbed count vs
table-expected count) is the remaining half and belongs with dotfiles-hwds.28 /
.29, not here.

title: qs-clip.sh/qs-notif.sh toggle: a screen-suffixed DISPLAY (:10.0) matches no instance, so $mod+v and $mod+n never open
design:
DISCOVERED while root-causing dotfiles-hwds.31, on the LIVE machine, 2026-07-28.

Independent of hotkeyd. cmd_toggle builds its session key straight out of the
environment:

    _want="DISPLAY=$DISPLAY"

and compares it against each live quickshell instance's own environ DISPLAY.
i3 on the xrdp session runs with DISPLAY=:10.0 (xrdp/xinitrc), while its own
quickshell instance carries the bare :10 (qs-start.sh). So the compare matches
NOTHING, and with both sessions live the script takes its refuse-rather-than-
guess branch and exits 1 without opening anything.

Measured on the live host:
    $ DISPLAY=:10.0 sh quickshell/qs-clip.sh toggle
    qs-clip.sh: 'DISPLAY=:10.0' matches no running instance, and 2 sessions
    are live (DISPLAY=:10 DISPLAY=:0 ) -- set QS_CLIP_DISPLAY to choose
    rc=1
    $ DISPLAY=:0.0 ... same on the native session (i3 there is :0.0 too)
i3 binding events confirm the bind fires and the exec runs; the picker window
never maps at all.

Masked until both sessions are up: with exactly ONE live quickshell instance
cmd_toggle falls back to it, so the mismatch is invisible.

store_dir() has normalized the screen suffix since 544d7877; cmd_toggle was
never given the same treatment -- the two halves of the same script disagree
about what a session key is.

NOTE the normalization must strip only a trailing .<digits>: ${DISPLAY%.*}
would maul a host-qualified display (example.com:0 -> example).
notes:
DISCOVERY id: dotfiles-56eh (consolidate the display-normalization idiom, P3, discovered-from sxg1).

AUDITED 2026-07-28: REJECTED (production fix is CORRECT and should stay in main; the gap is test-suite stability in test-notif-history.sh only).

VERIFIED GOOD -- do not redo:

title: hotkeyd closes quickshell overlays — $mod+n and $mod+v dismiss themselves after ~3s
design:
USER-REPORTED, reproduced and root-caused, 2026-07-28. $mod+n (notifications)
and $mod+v (clipboard picker) "seem not working" while $mod+w still works.

NOT a bind problem. i3's binds fire correctly -- subscribing to i3 binding
events while injecting shows symbol=n -> exec qs-notif.sh and symbol=v -> exec
qs-clip.sh, both dispatched. The scripts run clean standalone (rc 0). The
picker WINDOW opens: i3's tree goes 7 -> 8 windows.

THE PICKER THEN CLOSES ITSELF after ~3 seconds. Timed:

    t=0     7 windows
    t=+0.3  8   <- picker mapped
    t=+1    8
    t=+2    8
    t=+4    7   <- gone, nobody asked
    t=+7    7

HOTKEYD IS THE CAUSE. Controlled experiment, same display, same script:

    daemon RUNNING  -> picker gone by t=+4s
    daemon STOPPED  -> picker still open at t=+6s   (8 windows throughout)

Stopping the daemon is sufficient to fix it; starting it reintroduces it.

WHY $mod+w IS UNAFFECTED, which is the clue to the mechanism: the task switcher
is driven by quickshell/qs-keymon.py reading raw XI2 events, and i3 holds only a
`nop` grab to stop the key leaking. It never opens an overlay window. $mod+n and
$mod+v both open a quickshell overlay that takes focus and (per qs-clip.sh's
header) a keyboard grab. So the failure is specific to overlays that grab.

LIKELY MECHANISM, unproven: the overlay takes an active keyboard grab when it
opens; hotkeyd's XI2 passive grabs interact with that -- either the overlay's
grab fails and it dismisses itself, or hotkeyd's grab set is re-synced (it
re-grabs on layer transitions and on XI_HIERARCHY_CHANGED / XI_DEVICE_CHANGED)
and that disturbs the overlay's grab or its focus. The ~3s delay is suspicious
and worth measuring against the daemon's own timers -- it is close to nothing in
hotkeyd's known intervals (0.25s idle select, 1s heartbeat, 120ms release
guard), so the delay may belong to the overlay's own dismiss-on-focus-loss.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is a REGRESSION IN DAILY USE introduced by arming autostart
(a76e9a9). Every suite is green; the nav cutover works; and two everyday
features silently broke. It was found only because the user tried to use their
own machine.

FIRST DIAGNOSTIC STEP: run the overlay with hotkeyd running and capture whether
its XGrabKeyboard succeeds or returns AlreadyGrabbed / is broken by a subsequent
hotkeyd re-grab. hotkeyd's transition log (dotfiles-hwds.27, merged) now records
every grab re-sync, so correlate the picker's dismiss timestamp against it.

ALSO CHECK against dotfiles-hwds.30: :0 has a STUCK exclusive keyboard grab
whose holder was never identified, and quickshell was ruled out there only by a
restart. If hotkeyd disturbs overlay grabs, the two may be the same underlying
interaction seen from opposite ends -- one where the overlay dies, one where its
grab outlives it.

WORKAROUND for the user meanwhile: `hotkeyd.sh stop :10` restores $mod+n and
$mod+v (and loses nav). $mod+Shift+r (panic) does the same and also hands nav
back to i3, which is the better trade.

title: hold on $mod+Shift+s flickers the aiming layer - bind fires on press, no single-instance guard
design:
Found during live :0/:10 smoke of sp024 (human-reported, 2026-08-01).

SYMPTOM. Holding $mod+Shift+s makes the bar strip and focus ring flicker in
and out repeatedly. Expected: one entry into the aiming phase per physical
gesture.

EVIDENCE.
- hotkeyd/cmd/hotkeyd/config.go:405 declares the bind WITHOUT OnRelease, so it
  fires on PRESS. Its two siblings at 403-404 ($mod+Print, $mod+Shift+Print)
  both already carry OnRelease: true. This bind is the odd one out.
- hotkeyd/cmd/hotkeyd/daemon.go:705 DOES suppress auto-repeat (drops any press
  carrying XIKeyRepeat, one action per physical press), so a missing repeat
  guard is NOT the cause.
- quickshell/qs-screenshot.sh has NO single-instance guard - no flock, no
  pgrep, no pidfile. N overlapping instances are possible.
- Each instance raises set-layer screenshot at start and runs an unconditional
  set-layer default on EVERY exit path. Instance N exiting therefore clears the
  layer instance N+1 just raised. That is the flicker.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, NOT PROVEN. Reported on the xrdp :10 session. ft011 records
that xrdp injects at device level and synthesises Shift around every character;
repeats there plausibly arrive as fresh presses WITHOUT the XIKeyRepeat flag,
sliding past the daemon.go:705 guard. Needs confirmation by observing the flag
on a real held chord on :10, and by checking whether :0 flickers too. If :0 is
clean, the xrdp-injection path is confirmed as the trigger.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT CAUSED BY sp024. Before the cutover the same overlap ran
i3-msg mode default on exit and raced identically. sp024 made it VISIBLE.

FIX DIRECTION, two parts - the first alone is not sufficient.
1. Add OnRelease: true to the $mod+Shift+s bind, matching its siblings and
   us019 AC2. One launch per physical gesture.
2. Add a single-instance guard to qs-screenshot.sh so a second launch while one
   is live exits WITHOUT running the layer clear. Without this, any double-fire
   still flickers - and ft011 documents that xrdp can yield two releases for one
   physical press, so OnRelease alone can double-fire on that session.

TEST. A regression case driving two overlapping launches must show the layer
raised once and cleared once, never cleared while a live instance holds it.
close_reason: Fixed in 478f0938. Two-part fix: OnRelease on the $mod+Shift+s bind (matching its two siblings) plus a session-scoped pid ownership token in qs-screenshot.sh so a superseded launcher declines to clear. New suite quickshell/test-screenshot-launcher.sh, mutation-verified: fails against the pre-fix launcher with a trailing extra clear, passes after. Golden-dump parity kept honest via an explicit divergence allowlist plus a guard test rejecting stale entries, rather than editing the frozen python fixture. Live-confirmed working by the human on :10.

Branch bd-dotfiles-1m4t.6.0 | commit 26486e17 | worktree /home/jan/.dotfiles/.worktrees/bd-dotfiles-1m4t.6.0

THREADING HANDOFF (matched, not invented). The existing pattern was already
there: hotkeyd_layer_monitor is a daemon reader thread that marshals to the
GLib main thread via GLib.idle_add. Previously it computed the boolean itself
and sent GLib.idle_add(_set_layer_colored, layer_colours_ring(layer)). Now it
sends GLib.idle_add(_set_layer_state, layer) -- the NAME -- and _set_layer_state
(main-thread-only, same discipline as i3_mode_colored/layer_colored/mode_colored)
decides both colour and suppression. No queue, no new primitive, one line
changed in the loop.

CRITERIA
- SUPPRESS_LAYERS = {'screenshot-drag'} (qs-focus-border.py:102). _set_layer_state
  arms mode_suppressed BEFORE border.hide() (arming first closes the window in
  which an in-flight refresh could restack after the hide); leaving unsuppresses
  and refreshes via 'if recolored or was_suppressed' -- the was_suppressed arm
  exists because leaving a suppress layer changes no COLOUR, so a colour-only
  guard would never bring the border back.
- Suppression wins over colour: layer_colours_ring gained 'and layer not in
  SUPPRESS_LAYERS'. Every other non-default non-silent layer unchanged.
- i3-side retired as DELETIONS: SUPPRESS_MODES gone (asserted by
  'not hasattr(qsb, "SUPPRESS_MODES")', so an emptied-but-present set fails),
  binding-event pre-arm branch gone, and the mode branch no longer touches
  mode_suppressed at all -- it neither arms nor disarms. 'screenshot' stays in
  COLOR_MODES.
- Feed loss: socket-loss fallback now sends 'default' (was: False), clearing
  suppression AND colour.
- Replay-on-connect: covered on the WIRE, not by assumption -- a real AF_UNIX
  server whose FIRST line is screenshot-drag, with the real hotkeyd_layer_monitor
  reading it in a real thread.
- ModeBarTheme.qml: mapping KEPT, comment rewritten to say it resolves the
  DAEMON layer name (Bar.qml activeMode prefers a non-default daemonLayer) and
  why both arms must land on one registry key (unbroken strip through the gesture).

INTERLEAVING ORDER -- PROVEN BOTH WAYS (the edge case that drove the design).
The i3 mode and the layer are cleared by two unordered subprocess calls out of
the same qs-screenshot.sh cleanup.
  Order A (i3 mode default FIRST, layer second): asserts the i3 clear does NOT
  unsuppress and does NOT redraw while the layer is still up, then the layer
  clear ends unsuppressed/uncoloured/refreshed.
  Order B (layer default FIRST, i3 mode second): layer clear unsuppresses and
  redraws; mode clear then ends unsuppressed/uncoloured/refreshed.
Order A is what forced 'no i3 mode may disarm suppression'. MUTANT M2 (restore
mode_suppressed=False in the mode branch, i.e. the pre-sp023 shape) kills

title: [bug] qs-clip.sh candidates() probes every quickshell pid with an unbounded ipc call — one stale instance wedges the picker permanently
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (measured live on :10, 2026-07-31)

candidates() in quickshell/qs-clip.sh asked EVERY process named quickshell
what IPC targets it exposes, with no timeout, inside a $(...) command
substitution.

qs-start.sh (run by the $mod+Shift+r hammer, i3/config.common:484) had left
an 18-hour-old quickshell instance behind (pid 3648371) whose ipc socket
accepted but never answered: 'timeout 2 quickshell ipc --pid 3648371 show'
returned rc=143 (killed), while the other three instances answered in ms. One
unbounded probe => the substitution never returns => cmd_toggle never gets a
candidate list at all, so $mod+Shift+v silently did nothing.

Self-amplifying: a stuck 'quickshell ipc' client is itself a process named
quickshell, so pgrep -x handed the corpses back on the next press. Observed
state before cleanup: 43 wedged qs-clip.sh toggle shells + 26 parked ipc
clients, each keypress with more corpses to probe than the last. No recovery
without killing them by hand.

FIX  timeout "$IPC_T" (QS_CLIP_IPC_TIMEOUT, default 3) on the probe, plus an
explicit skip of pids whose cmdline contains ' ipc ' — a one-shot client verb,
never a shell that could host the picker. The skip precedes the environ read
so this script's own probes are never probed recursively.

REGRESSION TEST  new scenario in quickshell/test-clip-history.sh, 4 asserts.
Instruments: a copy of /usr/bin/sleep named 'quickshell' (so pgrep -x matches)
holding a DISPLAY in its environ, plus a PATH shim named 'quickshell' that
hangs for 'ipc --pid <that pid> show' and delegates everything else to the
real binary. Toggle is bounded by 'timeout 25' so a regression reports instead
of hanging the suite.
  RED before fix: rc=124 (hung), no picker opened.
  GREEN after: returns, opens on the live session, no parked client left.
  Suite went 84 pass/3 fail -> 88 pass/3 fail; the 3 are pre-existing
  (dotfiles-odfr, identical on HEAD).
Fix Status: FIXED
- commit d444f76
- test-clip-history.sh: 88 passed / 3 failed; the 4 new asserts all pass
- RED evidence: rc=124 (hung) + no picker on the pre-fix script
- baseline on HEAD before the change: 84 passed / 3 failed, identical failure set => the 3 are pre-existing (dotfiles-odfr)
- live evidence on :10: toggle now returns in 0s and opens the picker with a zombie quickshell present (2387034, Zs) that the old code would have probed
Trigger attribution refined (see dotfiles-rxlj for the measurement): i3
'reload' does NOT re-run exec_always on this build, but $mod+Shift+r
(i3/config.common:484) execs qs-start.sh DIRECTLY as part of the binding, so
the orphaned-quickshell half of this bug does ride that chord. Unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] clip-sync.sh has no display arg and no flock guard — a test-display instance silently owns the job and :10 PRIMARY stops mirroring
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (measured live on :10, 2026-07-31)

Two defects, one file (i3/scripts/clip-sync.sh):

1. NO STARTUP SEED — the clobber the user reported as 'clipboard from
   windows is broken / paste gives old text'. Last-seen PRIMARY ($A) and
   CLIPBOARD ($B) were seeded EMPTY, so the first loop tick read PRIMARY,
   found it != empty i.e. 'changed', and published that stale selection over
   the CLIPBOARD. wsl.conf starts the loop from exec_always and $mod+Shift+r
   (i3/config.common:484) is 'reload' — so every press of the hammer chord
   reverted the clipboard to whatever PRIMARY last held.
   Measured: clipboard held FRESH-A-8891; one second after the loop restarted
   it held an hours-old kubectl terminal selection.

2. NO DISPLAY ARG, NO FLOCK — why it stayed broken. clip-sync.sh trusted an
   inherited $DISPLAY and had no single-instance guard, alone in the clip
   family (clip-store/clip-img-bridge/clip-set/clip-feed all take an explicit
   display + per-display flock). A leftover harness instance from an earlier
   agent session was running with DISPLAY=:89 (fd 1 -> /tmp/claude-1000/i389.log,
   started Jul 30 19:04) and was the ONLY clip-sync alive: it mirrored a dead
   Xvfb while :10's PRIMARY never updated. Invisible, because pgrep still
   showed a live loop. The old launcher's 'pkill -f clip-sync\\.sh$' also could
   not tell one session's loop from another's.

FIX
  clip-sync.sh: display is $1 (or CLIP_SYNC_DISPLAY), missing -> exit 78;
  every xclip call names it explicitly; per-display flock on
  $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/clip-sync.<display>.lock, loser exits 0; children close
  fd 9; last-seen state SEEDED from the live selections before the loop, with
  the CLIPBOARD authoritative (an explicit copy is never overwritten by a
  drag-selection; an empty clipboard has nothing to lose so PRIMARY seeds).
  wsl.conf: 'clip-sync.sh :10', pkill removed (flock replaces it).

REGRESSION TEST  i3/scripts/test-clip-sync.sh (new, 15 asserts, Xvfb)
  RED before fix: 8 fail. GREEN after: 15/15.
  Mutation check: deleting only the seed block (anchor verified by line delta)
  turns the startup scenario red — FRESH-CLIPBOARD replaced by STALE-PRIMARY,
  the exact production symptom. So the assertion is not vacuous.
  Every loop the suite starts is handed DISPLAY=:77 (nonexistent) with the
  real display as an argument, so a loop that trusts the env fails the suite.
Fix Status: FIXED
- commit 800e56d
- regression suite i3/scripts/test-clip-sync.sh: 15/15 PASS (rc=0, no leaked owners)
- RED evidence: 8/15 failed on the pre-fix script
- mutation evidence: seed block deleted (anchor verified by line delta) => startup scenario red, FRESH-CLIPBOARD replaced by STALE-PRIMARY
- live evidence on :10: clipboard held LIVE-PROOF-explicit-copy with a stale PRIMARY; after starting the fixed loop CLIP unchanged, PRIMARY converged
- test-clip-integration.sh unaffected: failure set byte-identical with and without the wsl.conf change (10 pre-existing, dotfiles-egxb)
CORRECTION to the root-cause note above (trigger attribution only; the defect
and the fix are unchanged and verified).

I originally wrote that $mod+Shift+r reverted the clipboard on every press,
reasoning that exec_always re-runs on i3 reload. MEASURED, it does not:

  probe: printf 'exec_always --no-startup-id touch /tmp/marker' > ~/.i3/config.d/zzz-probe.conf
         i3-msg reload  ->  marker NOT created  (overlay then removed, reloaded again)
  corroborating: 'i3-msg reload' spawned no clip-sync at all, and i3's child
  list (pgrep -P 888) was byte-identical before and after.

So on this build exec_always re-runs on i3 'restart' ($mod+Shift+c,
i3/config:81) and not on 'reload' ($mod+Shift+r, i3/config.common:484, which
does its own hotkeyd + qs-start.sh execs — that half is why the picker bug
dotfiles-03ym rode the same chord).

The clobber therefore fired on $mod+Shift+c and on every hand/agent restart
of the daemon, which is how the reported symptom kept recurring. The clobber
I measured live was from my own manual start of the loop.

Live verification at the real trigger, after the fix: with PRIM=STALE and
CLIP=FRESH-explicit-copy-4471, running the SHIPPED command string lifted from
wsl.conf in i3's own environment (the same thing an i3 restart does) left
CLIP=FRESH-explicit-copy-4471 and converged PRIM onto it. Loop 2743765 alive.

Side observation, not this issue: every clip daemon running on the host was a
ppid=1 leftover from agent session f8dc51f8 (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in the
environ), including 'clip-store.sh :10' whose own DISPLAY was :87 — it works
only because the explicit-display contract makes the argument win. None were
i3-parented. Also ~/.i3/config.d/ links only wsl.conf; zz-fallback-binds.conf
is not linked on this host.
LIVE VERIFICATION AT THE REAL TRIGGER ($mod+Shift+c), post-fix.

First, the two facts the earlier correction rested on, both probed with a
throwaway 'exec_always ... touch <marker>' overlay in ~/.i3/config.d/:
  i3-msg reload   -> marker NOT created  (reload does not re-run exec_always)
  i3-msg restart  -> marker created      (restart does)
  xdotool alt+shift+c -> marker created  (the chord really does reach i3)

Test 1, flock path (incumbent loop alive):
  CLIP=MARKER-C1-survives-restart-9910 -> $mod+Shift+c -> unchanged, PRIMARY
  converged. Loop pid unchanged (the restart's instance lost the flock and
  exited 0, which is the designed outcome). i3 pid 888 and all 18 windows
  preserved across the restart.

Test 2, seed path (no incumbent — the pre-fix clobber scenario exactly):
  loop killed, then PRIM=STALE-primary-old-drag-2200,
                    CLIP=FRESH-copy-must-survive-restart-7788
  $mod+Shift+c -> CLIP unchanged, PRIM converged onto the explicit copy,
  and exec_always started a fresh loop 2772688 with ppid=888 — i3-parented,
  unlike every clip daemon that was running before this work (all ppid=1
  leftovers from agent session f8dc51f8).

Pre-fix, this second sequence is the one that reverted the clipboard.
close_reason: Closed

and dotfiles-ylmp.15's success_criteria names only HOTKEYD_BIN +
HOTKEYD_PROC_PAT/HAS_BINDS_FLAG. Neither mentions HOTKEYD_ENGINE_DEFAULT=go,
which the launcher-driven stages REQUIRE: without it hotkeyd.sh's engine_for()
falls through to its python default and starts PYTHON daemons while

    same + HOTKEYD_ENGINE_DEFAULT=go                ->  63 passed, 0 failed
Exactly reproduces the implementer's logged deviation. Fails LOUDLY (9 named
FAILs, exit 1), so it cannot produce a false green — the cost is debugging
time and a misleading 'the go engine fails the panic contract' verdict.

#### why it matters now
The human's live :10 cutover verification and dotfiles-ylmp.16 both re-run
this matrix. This is the trap most likely to bite them.

Add HOTKEYD_ENGINE_DEFAULT=go to the documented invocation in
test-hotkeyd.sh's header, to test-engine.sh (which owns the engine-capability
seam), and to test-panic.sh / test-launcher.sh headers. State plainly WHY:
the launcher resolves the engine per display and the suites' pgrep pattern
must agree with what the launcher actually starts.

#### note
The incomplete header line predates dotfiles-ylmp.15 (commit ee24e9005).

title: (BUG) web tier crash guard loops forever on OOM-after-load; fallback text unreachable
description:
The T5 crash guard in preview/qml/WebTier.qml is meant to be "renderer
terminated -> reload ONCE -> else fallback text, never a dead window". For a
renderer that OOMs AFTER the page has loaded successfully, it instead loops
forever and the fallback text is unreachable.

MECHANISM (preview/qml/WebTier.qml:84-88 vs :95-112):

    onLoadingChanged: if (status === LoadSucceededStatus) root._crashCount = 0
    onRenderProcessTerminated: { _crashCount++
        if (_crashCount <= 1) reloadTimer.start() else _failed = true }

An OOM-after-load ALWAYS follows a LoadSucceededStatus, so _crashCount is
reset to 0 on every iteration and can never reach 2. Sequence:
  load ok -> _crashCount=0 -> JS grows -> OOM -> _crashCount=1 -> reload
  -> load ok -> _crashCount=0 -> OOM -> ... forever
_failed never flips, so the "web content crashed and did not recover" Text
never appears. The one-reload guard only bounds crashes that happen BEFORE
load completes.

MEASURED (own xorgxrdp :26, ceiling active, a page retaining ~500 MB of JS):
- 59 "web tier renderer terminated (status=3 code=5)" lines and climbing at
  ~0.5/s; renderer child pid churned 80340 -> 97587 -> 97915 -> 98175 ->
  98537 -> 99441 -> 99693 -> ... one new renderer per crash.
- Zero occurrences of the fallback text.
- The window shows the page perpetually restarting (screenshot: stuck at
  "step 12/20" forever), which is worse UX than the intended crash text.

IT SURVIVES A WINDOW RESTART. preview-d restores the slot's last URL, so
`preview window 1 --close` then `preview window 1` re-loads the offending URL
and resumes the loop (verified: freshly spawned window had 4 terminations
within 8 s). The only escape is previewing a different file.

WHY NOW: sp022 T10 sets --js-flags=--max-old-space-size=256 on every display.
That lowers the renderer's heap ceiling from V8's RAM-derived ~1.33 GB (on a
24 GB host) to 256 MB, which makes OOM-after-load a REACHABLE state for
content that previously rendered fine. Same 500 MB page, same rig:
  pre-fix wrapper : 0 terminations, page completes ("SETTLED, still alive")
  with T10's fix  : 10 terminations in 30 s, never completes
So T10 did not create this guard bug, but it converted it from unreachable to
reachable for any web content whose live JS heap lands between 256 MB and
~1.33 GB.

FIX DIRECTIONS (pick with evidence):
- Do not reset _crashCount on LoadSucceededStatus alone; reset it only on a
  genuinely new sourceUrl (onSourceUrlChanged already does), or gate the
  reset on the load having been stable for some interval, or count crashes
  per-URL within a time window.
- Consider whether the restored-URL behaviour should skip auto-restore for a
  URL that crash-looped.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED: slow OOM-after-load loop is bounded; guard now classifies self-inflicted OOM by termination STATUS and layers a never-refunded lifetime cap + exponential backoff. Branch bd-dotfiles-f532.0, commit e716bd4.

FILES
- preview/qml/CrashPolicy.js (new) — pure reducer: newState / isSelfInflicted / backoffMs / onTerminated / onProbationElapsed / failText
- preview/qml/WebTier.qml — wires the Qt signals to it, owns the two timers
- nushell/actions/preview-test — test 33 (11 cases + purity + fallback-text)
- preview/README.md — new '## Web-tier crash recovery' section replaces the stale bounded-fast/unbounded-slow paragraph

DESIGN (and why the alternatives lose)
exitCode does NOT need to be the discriminator; terminationStatus already is (see the DEVIATION note above for the measured table). A per-URL cumulative cap tight enough to stop the loop (3-4) breaks R4's four-kill recovery; loose enough for R4 lets the loop run minutes; a rolling window fails identically — all confirmed by the fact that the slow loop's 17.8 s period and R4's 14 s spacing are the same shape. Status-based classification dissolves the ambiguity. Backoff alone does NOT stop the loop (proved: with the classifier stubbed out, backoff only decays the rate); the never-refunded LIFETIME_BUDGET=8 is what makes 'cannot loop' unconditional. Budgets: OOM 1 (never refunded), transient 1 (refunded after 10 s probation), lifetime 8 (never refunded). Line: gives up on the 2nd self-inflicted OOM, a 2nd crash inside one probation window, or the 9th termination of any cause; any re-preview is a clean slate.

AFTER 2 terminations (t=17, t=35), then flat for the remaining 165 s, failed=true reason=oom, fallback text on screen, renderer not respawned (renderer sample empty from t=36 to t=199).
- fast shape: 2 terminations (t=3, t=7) before AND after — sp022 T10's result preserved, 2 distinct renderer pids total.
- DEGRADED (isSelfInflicted stubbed to false, i.e. the classification stops matching on a future Qt): 9 terminations at t=17/35/54/74/95/121/155/203/252 with reload delays 0/1k/2k/4k/8k/16k/30k/30k then fail(lifetime) — bounded, visibly decaying, fallback shown.

- R1 new URL clears _failed: fallback up at t=44 (transient2/oom2/lifetime2, reason=oom); sourceUrl switched at t=45 -> all counters 0, failed=false, new page LoadSucceeded and healthy for 30 s.
- R2 window restart: preview-d's restore is server.go:360 (ws connect replays slots.CurrentPath) — unchanged and unaware of crashes, so the slow URL DOES re-arm on restart, but a fresh client on that URL now costs exactly 2 terminations then the fallback (that is literally the 'fixed-slow' run above: a fresh qml6 on the offending URL). Bounded, same as T10's fast-case R2. No daemon-side change needed.
- R3 one SIGKILL on a healthy page: exactly 1 termination (status=2 code=9), reload in 0 ms, LoadSucceeded, no fallback, transient refunded to 0 after probation.
- R4 four SIGKILLs 14 s apart: all four recovered (LoadSucceeded after each), delays 0/1000/2000/4000 ms, oom=0, lifetime=4 of 8, failed=false throughout.

Deviations: one, logged above (exitCode/status discrimination premise was wrong).

title: sp022 T10: bound the web tier's per-navigation memory growth (dotfiles-j5kq)
design:
#### type
task

#### effort
3h

#### depends
9

#### why this is epic scope, not a detached backlog bug
sp022's stated deliverable is a LONG-LIVED, one-window preview client. T9's
E2E gate proved the identity half of that promise holds (one pid, one window
id, no engine reload — verified twice, independently). It also proved the
LIFETIME half does not: the web tier grows ~32-48 MB on every akm navigation
and never releases it. Closing the epic as done with that unfixed would
record a completion the product does not have, so the leak is pulled into
the epic rather than left to compete in the backlog.

#### files_touched
preview/qml/WebTier.qml, preview/qml/PreviewView.qml (web tier navigation /
history handling), possibly nushell/actions/preview (the
QTWEBENGINE_CHROMIUM_FLAGS the wrapper already composes for xrdp, ~line 239),
preview/README.md (document whatever bound ends up guaranteed)

#### success_criteria
- **Same-URL re-navigation is bounded:** the reviewer's akm loop
  (page.html <-> docs/notes/adr0009.md, the SAME akm URL, x20) shows PSS
  reaching a PLATEAU rather than ~32 MB/visit linear growth. Reference
  numbers to beat: 471 MB at iter 1 -> 1102 MB at iter 20, zero delta decay.
- **The seven-tier sweep is bounded:** the T9 criterion-1 sweep shape
  (image -> md -> code -> .d2 -> html -> akm -> stl -> image, x25) ends
  within a stated ceiling instead of 561 MB -> 1769 MB with no plateau.
  A documented, justified ceiling is acceptable; unbounded growth is not.
- **Identity is not regressed to buy the bound:** the same sweep still shows
  ONE pid, ONE X11 window id, and a STABLE set of engine child pids across
  every checkpoint — i.e. the fix must not work by tearing down and
  respawning the engine or the window. This is sp022's hard requirement and
  T9's criterion 1; re-verify it, do not assume it.
- **Both tiers still render:** screenshot-verified akm (the cross-origin
  akm-graph iframe actually drawn) and stl (WebGL) after the change, on an
  xorgxrdp display, since the swiftshader flag path is the same surface a
  flags-based fix would touch.
- Existing gates stay green: go test in preview/ + d2/router/ + akm-graph/,
  and nushell/actions/preview-test (31/31 today).

#### edge_cases
If the mechanism turns out to be Chromium's back-forward cache / retained
navigation history, a flags-only fix must be checked against the stl tier —
the wrapper's existing xrdp flags exist because Chromium's GPU blocklist
refused swiftshader (dotfiles-14kr), and stl is the tier that broke. Do not
regress it to fix memory. If no bound is achievable without recreating the
WebEngineView, that is a FINDING: say so with numbers and propose the
trade-off explicitly (a recreate-per-navigation fix trades the ~240 MiB
one-time engine cost and sp022's identity requirement for the bound, which
may not be worth it) rather than quietly breaking criterion 1.

#### test_plan
Reproduce first, then fix, then re-measure with the SAME scripts so the
before/after numbers are comparable. The reviewer's rig recipe (own
xorgxrdp display via /usr/lib/Xorg :NN -config xrdp/xorg.conf, own i3,
fresh binaries, isolated HOME, private ports) is recorded in
dotfiles-j5kq's notes and in T9's scratchpad RIG.md. Add a regression test
where one is expressible (the wrapper's spawn-env-prefix table already
table-tests flag composition, so a flags-based fix is unit-testable there).

Cause: sp022 T3 made a .d2 file's payload the compiled SVG bytes relayed from d2-router (relayD2SVG, preview/proxy.go:412), and T4 renders those bytes in a NATIVE Qt Quick Image (svgDelegate, preview/qml/PreviewView.qml). d2 v0.7.1 emits an OUTER <svg viewBox=...> wrapping an INNER <svg class="d2-... d2-svg"> — measured: 'curl 127.0.0.1:4800/api/svg?path=.../fixtures/svg/nested.d2 | grep -c "<svg"' = 2. Qt's SVG renderer implements SVG Tiny 1.2, which forbids nested <svg>, so it skips the inner element — i.e. it skips the ENTIRE drawing and renders only the empty outer canvas.

This is systematic, not fixture-specific: every d2 output has this shape, so the svg tier is blank for ALL .d2 files, on every display. The old wry/WebKitGTK host rendered d2 SVG through a browser engine (no Tiny 1.2 restriction), so this is a user-visible regression sp022 introduces.

Candidate fixes:
1. Strip/flatten the outer <svg> wrapper in relayD2SVG before relaying (server-side, keeps the native tier).
2. Route the svg tier to the WebTier (QtWebEngine) like html/akm/stl — costs the ~240 MiB web tier for diagrams.
3. Ask d2-router for un-nested output if d2 supports it.

title: sp022 integration risk: T6's xrdp software-backend forcing may break T5's web tier on :10 (the primary target display)
description:
Found by the scrum-master correlating two sp022 audits (2026-07-30). Not yet reproduced end-to-end — this is a predicted conflict with strong evidence on both sides.

SIDE A — T6 (dotfiles-zw0d.6, merged fe684d1) forces, on any xorgxrdp display:
  QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software
  LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1
per its success_criteria (adr0004/adr0005, i3/config-xrdp precedent). Display :10 IS xorgxrdp, and per sp022's own framing :10 is the primary target — 'the display where wry died'.

SIDE B — the T5 audit (dotfiles-zw0d.5, merged 0efcece) reports, while closing the stl/WebGL gap, that a working WebGL orbit required:
  QTWEBENGINE_CHROMIUM_FLAGS="--enable-unsafe-swiftshader --use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --disable-gpu-compositing"
and CRITICALLY that it worked *without* LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE / QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software, because that pair 'broke the whole Quick scenegraph in an earlier attempt'.

So the exact env T6 forces on :10 is the env the T5 audit found breaks rendering. If that holds on a real xorgxrdp session, then on the epic's primary display either the whole Quick scenegraph degrades (breaking ALL tiers, not just stl) or the web tier's WebGL content fails while native tiers survive. Both are user-visible regressions against the wry host sp022 replaces.

Caveats worth checking before assuming the worst: the T5 audit's breakage was observed on plain Xvfb with no GPU, which is not identical to xorgxrdp; and 'broke the scenegraph' may have been specific to combining those vars with the Chromium swiftshader flags rather than to the vars alone. T6's forcing predates the web tier existing, so nobody has run the combination.

Required work:
1. On a real :10 xorgxrdp session, launch the client through the T6 wrapper (which forces the pair) and sweep image -> md -> code -> html -> akm -> stl. Record which tiers render and which fail.
2. If the pair breaks anything, decide the fix: drop the forcing now that the client is Qt Quick rather than wry/WebKitGTK; or keep it for native tiers and inject the Chromium swiftshader flags for the web tier; or scope the forcing per tier.
3. Whatever wins, encode it in the wrapper + README and record the reasoning — adr0004/adr0005 justified the forcing for a different renderer, so a change here may warrant a new ADR at spec-retro.

title: d2-generated SVG's nested <svg> wrapper is unrenderable by Qt's SVG module (Tiny 1.2 profile)
design:
Discovered while empirically testing sp022 T4's svg native tier (PreviewView.qml). d2 v0.7.1 emits an outer wrapper <svg viewBox="0 0 W H"> containing an inner <svg class="d2-..." viewBox="..."> that holds ALL the actual diagram content (shapes/text/paths/mask). Qt's QtSvg image plugin implements the SVG Tiny 1.2 profile, which explicitly disallows nested <svg> elements — it logs 'qt.svg: Skipping a nested svg element, because SVG Document must not contain nested svg elements in Svg Tiny 1.2' and drops the ENTIRE inner content, rendering a blank/empty image.

Verified empirically:
- Fetched a live .d2's compiled svg via ft002's GET /api/svg (and preview-d's /file/<path>?native relay) — confirmed nested <svg><svg>...</svg></svg> structure.
- Loaded the raw bytes directly into a QML Image (file://, isolated from the whole preview-d/websocket pipeline) — status Ready but implicitWidth/implicitHeight report the OUTER svg's dimensions and the canvas renders blank.
- Manually flattened the svg (removed the outer wrapper tag, kept the inner one as root) and reloaded the identical Image element — renders perfectly (verified via screenshot: full alice/bob/carol diagram with arrows and labels, exactly as expected).

This isolates the bug to the SVG DOCUMENT SHAPE d2 emits, not to any QML/pan-zoom/live-reload code (PreviewView.qml's PannableStage component is otherwise fully verified correct: natural-size parsing via viewBox, zoom/fit math, and the 1s live-reload poll all work exactly as designed once fed a renderable svg).

Fix belongs server-side, most likely in d2/router's /api/svg handler or preview/proxy.go's relayD2SVG (sp022 T3): strip the outer wrapper <svg>...<svg core-content>...</svg></svg> down to just the inner <svg> (promoting its attributes to the root), OR flatten via a lightweight XML transform, before serving bytes to any QtSvg-based client. Needs a repo-wide check: does d2-view/BoardView.qml also hit this for real d2 boards, or does it only manifest for THIS specific compiled-svg shape? BoardView has apparently been working in production, so either d2's structure varies by diagram complexity, or BoardView's Image usage differs enough to dodge the same drop (worth checking BoardView against a real nested-svg board before assuming BoardView is exempt).

Impact: sp022 T4's svg/.d2 native tier is currently NON-FUNCTIONAL for any d2 board — the pan/zoom stage and live-reload poll all work, but the rendered image is blank. This blocks the epic's svg-tier success criteria until fixed.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED: flattenD2SVG (d2/router/svg_flatten.go), wired into writeSVG (d2/router/api.go) — the single point /api/svg writes bytes from, covering both the normal compiled-svg path and the last-good-fallback disk read.

WHERE + WHY (the "decide where" question): d2/router's /api/svg, not preview/proxy.go's relayD2SVG. Verified rather than assumed:
- relayD2SVG only forwards whatever bytes /api/svg returns (io.ReadAll + w.Write, unchanged) — fixing at the source means preview-d needs ZERO changes and automatically inherits the fix.
- d2/router and preview are separate Go modules (d2router / preview, checked go.mod) — no shared internal package exists today, and none is needed: there's exactly one producer (d2-router) and one pass-through consumer (preview-d) of these bytes right now, so a shared helper would be premature abstraction.
- Re the "/api/svg's contract is raw bytes" concern: flattening is behavior-preserving, not a mutation of the diagram — merged attributes keep every outer attribute the inner tag lacked (xmlns, xmlns:xlink, preserveAspectRatio, data-d2-version), so a browser renders flattened output identically to nested output. No consumer loses anything; Qt-based consumers gain renderability. That weakens the "contract violation" framing enough that fixing at the shared source, benefiting every current and future /api/svg consumer, wins over scoping the fix to preview's relay alone.
- Confirmed BoardView.qml (separate code path, never touches d2-router) is ALSO broken — see discovery below — which independently reinforces fixing as close to the SOURCE (d2's own svg emission surface, i.e. d2-router) as this task's scope allows, over a preview-only patch that a sibling bug (BoardView) couldn't reuse anyway.

ATTRIBUTE-PROMOTION DECISIONS (empirically verified, not guessed):
- Compiled 3 independent real d2 v0.7.1 sources (a synthetic 2-edge diagram, the committed fixtures/svg/nested.svg fixture, and the real production board auctions/solution/mindtime/docs/map/d2/01-context.svg, 67121 bytes) — all three share IDENTICAL outer-vs-inner attribute sets: outer={xmlns, xmlns:xlink, data-d2-version, preserveAspectRatio, viewBox}, inner={class, width, height, viewBox}.
- Root tag after flatten = inner's full attribute set (its viewBox wins — it carries the real content offset, e.g. "-691 -215 6143 1904" vs outer's plain "0 0 6143 1904") PLUS any outer attribute the inner lacked (xmlns, xmlns:xlink, preserveAspectRatio, data-d2-version). Verified via TestFlattenD2SVG_NestedWrapper_PromotesInnerToRoot.

UNIT EVIDENCE: go test ./... in d2/router — all pass, including 5 new tests (nested-wrapper promotion, idempotency on already-flattened output, generic non-d2 single-root svg left unchanged, 5 truncation/malformed sub-cases with panic recovery, non-svg bytes untouched). go vet clean, gofmt clean on all touched files. go test ./... in preview (unmodified) also green — no ffmpeg sandbox flakiness this run.

E2E EVIDENCE (real, not simulated):
- Built d2-router-d from this worktree, ran on isolated port 4899 (own svg cache dir, own child-port base — never touched shared pid 526113 or the since-restarted pid 3071842).
- GET /api/svg?path=<mindtime/01-context.d2> on MY router: 200, 67085 bytes (flattened from a genuinely fresh real compile, cache dir was empty before the request) — single <svg> root confirmed via byte inspection.
- qml6 Image harness (grabToImage — grabWindow() hangs indefinitely on this Qt 6.11.1 build under both xcb+Xvfb and offscreen; grabToImage on contentItem works reliably) on my own Xvfb :79 (never touched shared :10 per updated coordinator policy):

title: Discovered: hotkeyd-panic.sh target_displays() is hardcoded to python argv, blind to go daemons
design:
hotkeyd-panic.sh:133 discovers which displays currently have a daemon via a hardcoded pattern:

    pgrep -af 'hotkeyd\.py .*--display' 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*--display \(:[0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p'

target_displays() feeds panic's machine-wide stop loop (dotfiles-hwds.12's design: panic stops the daemon on EVERY display that has one, not just the caller's). dotfiles-ylmp.14 gave hotkeyd.sh's own daemon_pid() a dual-argv pattern (python hotkeyd.py OR go's bare hotkeyd binary, both keyed on --display) so stop/status can find and act on either engine's daemon regardless of the per-display engine table. hotkeyd-panic.sh's target_displays() was explicitly OUT of dotfiles-ylmp.14's files_touched (hotkeyd/dot.yaml, hotkeyd/hotkeyd.sh, hotkeyd/.gitignore only) and was intentionally left untouched.

Today this is dormant: dotfiles-ylmp.14 defaults every display to python, so no go daemon exists in production yet and target_displays() sees everything there is to see. It stops being dormant the moment a cutover task (dotfiles-ylmp.15 for :10, .16 for :0) flips a display's engine table entry to go: panic's blast-radius discovery would then silently miss that display's go daemon, so hotkeyd-panic.sh panic would relink the i3 fallback WITHOUT having stopped the go daemon underneath it -- reproducing exactly the CONTESTED state (two clients holding overlapping chords) the whole panic design exists to prevent, on the one display that was just cut over.

Fix shape (not designed here, flagging only): mirror hotkeyd.sh's daemon_pid() dual-argv regex in target_displays(), or factor a shared pattern the two scripts both read (hotkeyd.sh and hotkeyd-panic.sh already share the FALLBACK_LINK path and the linked() predicate convention -- this is the same kind of drift risk dotfiles-hwds.21's notes called out for that predicate).

Should land no later than the FIRST cutover task that flips a real display to go (dotfiles-ylmp.15), and arguably belongs in that task's scope since it is the thing that makes the cutover's blast radius (panic) safe. Filed here as discovered-from dotfiles-ylmp.14 rather than expanded into it, since ylmp.14's own files_touched explicitly excludes hotkeyd-panic.sh.

- The two call sites are not the same shape anyway: daemon_pid() is display-parameterised with a ( |$) boundary anchor; target_displays() is an unparameterised enumeration piped into sed. Only the argv core 'hotkeyd(\.py)?' is genuinely shared -- less than the scaffolding a shared file would cost.

title: Discovered: Go hotkeyd daemon does not exit when its X server dies (adr0014 fail-fast gap)
design:
Manually reproduced against the real ./cmd/hotkeyd binary (main branch as of bd-dotfiles-ylmp.11's landed daemon.go/main.go), outside any test harness pgrep-pattern ambiguity:

1. Started the go daemon via hotkeyd.sh (HOTKEYD_ENGINE_DEFAULT=go) against a throwaway Xvfb :191.
2. Confirmed the correct pid via a pattern anchored to the full binary path (not test-launcher.sh's broad HOTKEYD_PROC_PAT='hotkeyd', which false-positive-matched an unrelated shell wrapper in one run -- ruled out as a test artifact by re-running with an unambiguous pattern).
3. Killed the Xvfb process backing :191.
4. Waited 12s (same window test-launcher.sh's 'idle daemon exits when its X server dies (adr0014)' case allows). The go daemon (pid confirmed via /proc cmdline) was still alive at the end of the wait, then force-killed for cleanup.

python's hotkeyd.py exits ~1s after its X server dies in the same scenario (per test-launcher.sh's own comment and dotfiles history) -- both via the daemon's pending_events()/select-loop dual-observer design (adr0014). The go daemon does not reproduce this fail-fast behavior yet: it outlived its X server by >12s with nothing injected (an idle daemon, no events pumped, matching python's own worst-case test shape).

Found while validating dotfiles-ylmp.14 (build wiring / launcher engine selection) by running hotkeyd/test-launcher.sh with HOTKEYD_ENGINE_DEFAULT=go HOTKEYD_PROC_PAT='hotkeyd' -- that run showed 'the idle daemon outlived its X server by >12s' as a real (non-flaky, manually reproduced) failure, distinct from the --check/--health gaps which are dotfiles-ylmp.12's explicit in-progress scope.

This is a go-daemon behavioral gap (internal/x11 read-loop / daemon.go's idle/select path), not a launcher wiring issue -- dotfiles-ylmp.14's launcher correctly spawned, identified, and could stop the go daemon throughout. Relevant to whichever task runs the sp021 parity gate (dotfiles-ylmp.15) before any real display is cut over to go, since a daemon that outlives a dead X server is a resource leak at minimum and, per adr0014's stated rationale for this daemon family in general, a correctness expectation the epic explicitly designed for.

Shape: io.Pipe + newTestConn (io.Discard writer); go c.readLoop(); pw.Close(); <-c.done;

cannot be relied on to report loss on the first unchecked request after the server dies. The
latch is what makes the answer deterministic and named instead of buffering-dependent. That is
exactly the contract this task establishes ('every request path reports loss by name'), so
pinning it is strictly better than reverting it. Reverting (b) would leave XISelectEvents /
XIPassiveUngrabDevice returning nil on a dead connection.

ADJUDICATION — the substantive question: is the latch load-bearing?
  VERDICT: YES. The implementer's CONCLUSION is accepted and the prior
  reviewer's premise is rejected as incomplete. Option (a) was the right call.

  The prior reviewer argued: SendUnchecked registers no waiter -> cannot hang
  -> the latch is not required for fail-fast -> it merely renames a raw
  transport error. That reasoning has a hidden premise: that the TRANSPORT
  always reports the loss. It does not, on two independent grounds:

  1. The read loop can declare the connection lost while the WRITE side is
     still perfectly healthy. readLoop exits on ANY read error (read.go:87-92),
     not just peer death — e.g. the wrapped short-read error at read.go:149 or
     a truncated frame. In those states s.w.Write() genuinely returns nil, so
     without the latch XISelectEvents/XIPassiveUngrabDevice return nil on a
     connection the Conn has ALREADY declared dead. That is a literal false
     success, exactly the hazard the implementer named.

     *net.OpError/syscall.EPIPE and errors.Is(err, ErrConnLost) is FALSE. That
     breaks the invariant production prose states at read.go:10-15: 'ErrConnLost
     is what EVERY consumer of a Conn sees once the read loop has ended.'

     records a NIL return as a successful ungrab, so the false success is
     observable in the --health problems surface, not merely internal.
     read.go:80-85 also orders failAll BEFORE close(Events) with an explicit
     production comment stating this exact design intent: late requests must
     already be refused by the sequencer.

  wrong for this transport. 'A write lands in the kernel buffer and returns
  nil; only a later write gets EPIPE' is TCP behaviour. This client is
  unix-socket-only by construction (dial.go:38 net.Dial("unix"); open.go:23-25
  rejects remote displays outright), and on Linux AF_UNIX the peer's close sets
  our sk_shutdown, so the FIRST write after the X server exits does return
  EPIPE. The conclusion survives on grounds 1 and 2 above, which are stronger
  and transport-independent. NOTE (nit, follow-up, not a gap): the comment at
  read_test.go:300-304 restates the TCP mechanism and is inaccurate for a
  unix-only client; a future reader could use it to argue the latch away. The

  does error (ground 2). Not tautological, not manufactured.

via `smaps_rollup` incl. `QtWebEngineProcess` children (poc017 method
caveat: name-matched, approximate).

#### test_plan
This task IS the test; its artifacts are the scripts (swap-loop, sweep,
soak logger — throwaway, scratchpad, not repo code) and the recorded
numbers/window ids per stage. Pass = all four success_criteria rows hold
with evidence attached; any failure loops back to the owning task with the
reproduction script.

  clean+respawn, never signal a foreign pid).
- `pid-cmdline-matches` is replaced for windows by an exact-argument check:
  split `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` on NUL; require an element ending
  `PreviewView.qml` AND an element exactly `<N>` — slot 1's pidfile can no
  longer validate against slot 2's live window, and slot `2` never matches
  port `4200` (the `## problem` latent bug, closed and regression-tested).

  `place-window` uses `xdotool search --pid` → `[id=…]` under i3 and native

  `i3/config-xrdp` precedent); non-xrdp displays get neither.

Recycled pid whose cmdline is another qml6 app (d2-view!) → mismatch (no
`PreviewView.qml` arg), treated stale, never killed. Recycled pid that IS
another preview slot → mismatch on the exact `<N>` arg. Double `--close` →
idempotent. `bash -c … & echo $!` must yield the qml6 pid itself, not a
wrapper shell — verify `/proc/$pid/cmdline` right after spawn ([[poc016]]'s
harness trap: setsid/backgrounding returning the wrong pid). Display with
no Xorg at all (sway) → detection degrades to "not xrdp", no env forced.
`akm-root` failing → `~/.dotfiles` fallback; QML file missing there → loud
error naming the path.

file, temp-PATH pattern): spawn writes pidfile + passes `-- <N> <port>`;
second spawn no-ops; needle tests — stub with `PreviewView.qml 2 4200` args
does NOT validate slot 1's pidfile, DOES validate slot 2's; recycled-pid
stub without the QML arg → never signaled; `--close` terminates only the
verified pid; `stop` closes all windows. xrdp env test: fake /proc not
practical in nu — factor detection into a testable helper taking the
cmdline list (mirror the Rust seam) and table-test it.

title: sp022 T7: wrapper — docking collapse + live re-dock
design:
#### type
task

#### effort
6h

#### depends
6

#### files_touched
`nushell/actions/preview`, `nushell/actions/preview-test`,

- `prepare-split`, `wait-preview-mapped` (class poll), `finalize-dock`
  (move-the-terminal inversion), and `main-show`/`main-window`'s
  fresh-window-only guards are deleted — grep for their names returns
  nothing; docking is now: spawn → resolve window by pid (bounded poll) →
  mark the launching frame → `[<win>] move container to mark` + split/move
  the PREVIEW window into place — ordinary i3/sway, licensed by [[poc016]]
  (and [[poc017]] for the web tier).
- `preview show` re-docks a LIVE window: with window N already open,
  showing a landscape then a portrait image moves the SAME window (pid and
  window id unchanged) top then left — the README's "docks only on first
  open" limitation is removed, and the README updated to say so.
- `preview window [N]` still docks a fresh window beside the launching
  frame (right split default), and still degrades gracefully headless: no
  WM / no xdotool → spawn-only, no error (Termux stance preserved).
- Placement retry keeps the body-success-flag poll (i3-msg exits 0 while
  reporting `success: false` — the dotfiles-816 lesson stays encoded).

#### edge_cases
Window never maps (crashed qml6) → bounded poll expiry leaves a clear log
line, spawn error surfaced from wv-<N>.log tail, no hang. Launching frame
closed before finalize → mark gone → dock skipped, window stays where the
WM put it (best-effort stance). Re-dock while the web tier is live → the
engine window survives the reparent ([[poc017]]) — explicitly exercised.
Two `show` calls racing → second one's re-dock wins, no duplicate window
(pidfile no-op). sway: `[pid=…] move container to mark` verified — mark
syntax is shared, but run it, don't assume it.

#### test_plan
`preview-test`: assertions that the deleted helpers are gone and the
spawn-then-place path calls the fake WM binary with `[id=`/`[pid=` +
`mark`-based commands (fake i3-msg records its argv; success-flag JSON
stub). Manual E2E on `:10` (the display where wry died): fresh `show`
landscape → docked top; `show` portrait same window → re-docked left, same
window id via `xdotool`; repeat with an html path loaded (web tier live)
→ survives. WSL sway spot-check of the same flow.

title: sp022 T4: PreviewView.qml — window, ws client, native tiers
design:
#### type
task

#### effort
8h

#### depends
2, 3

#### files_touched
`preview/qml/PreviewView.qml` (new)

#### success_criteria
- `qml6 preview/qml/PreviewView.qml -- <N> <port>` opens an
  `ApplicationWindow` titled `preview <N>` that connects
  `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/preview<N>` (QtWebSockets), applies the priming
  frame, and hot-swaps a `Loader` delegate on every `{path, type}` frame —
  the ONE-window / no-respawn / no-engine-reload hard requirement, client
  half.
- Native delegates ship for `image` (`/file/<path>?full`, pan/zoom), `svg`
  (`?native` bytes via the same pan/zoom stage, `sourceSize` rasterization
  per the BoardView model), `md` (`Flickable` + `Text` MarkdownText over
  `?native` text), `code` (`Flickable` + monospace `Text` RichText over the
  `?native` fragment; unreadable-rich-text degrade path = plain text),
  `video` (poster `Image` at `/file/<path>`), `none` (fallback message).
  `html|akm|stl` route to the Task 5 web tier (until then: fallback text).
- svg delegate live-reloads: 1 s poll of its URL, byte-length compare,
  cache-busting token bump (the BoardView pattern over HTTP) — an edit to
  the watched `.d2` repaints without any window action.
- ws reconnect with backoff (shell app.js behavior preserved): daemon
  restart → client re-attaches and re-primes, process never exits on
  connection loss.
- Bad args (`N` non-numeric, missing port) → usage message on stderr +
  nonzero exit, no stack trace.

#### edge_cases
Frame arrives while previous delegate still loading → last-wins, no
stacking (Loader source swap). Same path re-broadcast → repaint is
idempotent (no flicker loop). Empty/`none` type → fallback text, never a
blank window. Image larger than 8192px → sourceSize clamp (BoardView
precedent). md with embedded HTML → MarkdownText renders what it can,
never executes script (no engine in this tier). ws frame with unknown
future type string → fallback delegate, not a crash. `kill -TERM` → clean
exit 0 (wrapper `--close` contract).

#### test_plan
Manual, scripted where possible (QML has no unit harness here — the repo
precedent is BoardView): launch against live daemon on `:10`; `preview
send` an image → fit-to-window render; send md → text render; send code →
highlighted or readable-mono text (record which); send `.d2` → svg pans;
edit the `.d2` → repaint within ~2 s; kill daemon → window stays, restart →
re-attaches; `xdotool search --pid` resolves the window; `xprop` confirms
title `preview <N>`. A swap-loop script (alternate image/md POSTs ×50)
shows one pid, one window id throughout — the hard requirement, measured.
notes:
Retry 2 implementer reported ready: commit 2b10b4b stacked on 1199f21 (+97/-45). Both sync XHRs unified into ONE async poll() with three guards (last-wins url check, _pendingUrl in-flight guard, lastLen===-1 first-response separation); unused Layouts import removed; explicit id:svgTier replaces a bare 'parent' that had been resolving to the Loader rather than the delegate Item. Measured on Xvfb :77 with private router/preview-d ports: 42 svg frames x2 runs (fast + 3s-blocking relay), DEATHS=0 FAIL=0, pid and window id constant, WM_NAME 'preview 3'. Live-reload 265ms detect, 17105->20032 bytes, token 0->1. Last-wins observed firing 3x. Anti-pile-up: 12 requests over a 44s soak on a 3s relay, not 44.

HONEST GAP the implementer flagged: it could NOT reproduce the pre-fix process death (0 deaths in 22 trials / 66 frames). Likely cause is MY mid-task display policy change — its runs were on Xvfb with NO WM, while the original audit measured 2/6 deaths on :10 (xorgxrdp + WM). So the death A/B is unproven; what IS measured is the named mechanism: identical 100ms heartbeat probe, sync = 42 beats in 21.7s with max GUI stall 6046ms (five >500ms), async = 227 beats in 22.6s with max stall 104ms (none >500ms). A multi-second GUI-thread block once per second is a defect on its own terms, and the original audit independently measured 0/8 with async. Reviewer must rule on whether stall-mechanism evidence substitutes for death-rate A/B.

Also for T6: bad-args usage line reaches stderr ONLY with QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1; without it rc=2 and NO output. Discovery filed: dotfiles-qnpk (preview-d relay auto-spawns d2-router-d from PATH on failed health probe; stale binary -> silent 404s, unhealthy port -> ~11.2s per request — the worst case the sync XHR blocked on).
close_reason:
AUDITED: APPROVED (retry 2, commit 2b10b4b on 1199f21)

RULING ON THE UNREPRODUCED DEATH A/B: the gap is CLOSED — the reviewer
reproduced it directly, so approval does NOT rest on stall-mechanism
inference. Root cause: the sync XHR blocked the GUI thread 4.5s+, so the
client stopped answering _NET_WM_PING (Qt advertises it: WM_PROTOCOLS =
WM_DELETE_WINDOW, WM_TAKE_FOCUS, _NET_WM_PING, _NET_WM_SYNC_REQUEST). A
ping-aware WM answers a ping timeout by closing the window, which makes Qt
exit CLEANLY = the original 'rc=0, window gone' signature, and explains the
~1-in-3 rate. i3 has no _NET_WM_PING atom and bare Xvfb has no WM, which is
why neither the implementer's runs nor the reviewer's first 6 i3 trials saw a
death. All on the reviewer's own Xvfb :82; ':10' never touched.

DIRECT A/B (identical harness, 3s-blocking relay, mutter-style ping watchdog):
  pre-fix (sync)  -> missed 20/15/15 pings, max ping reply 4.52-4.54s,
                     WM_DELETE_WINDOW -> DEAD rc=0, window gone .......... 3/3
  post-fix (async)-> 0 missed of 30, max ping reply 0.051-0.053s,
                     ALIVE, 1 window ................................... 4/4
  control: pre-fix + watchdog observe-only -> alive (unresponsiveness real)
  control: pre-fix on FAST relay + watchdog armed -> 0 missed, alive
           (the relay blocking is the cause, not the file)

CRITERIA VERIFIED:
- ONE window / no respawn / no engine reload: 8 type swaps
  (image->svg->md->code->html->code->svg->image) in one process — pid 3219720
  and window 0x60000e constant, windows=1 at every checkpoint, WM_NAME exactly
  "preview 3", _NET_WM_PID matching. Zero QML errors/warnings for the whole
  sweep (no binding loops, no TypeErrors).
- Native delegates all render (screenshots): image fit-to-window at true 3:2;
  svg a REAL diagram (o3b7's writeSVG flattening landed — single <svg>, 18182
  bytes, no longer blank); md as MarkdownText (heading/bold/italic/link/
  bullets); code with GENUINE chroma highlighting (keywords, strings, idents
  in distinct colours, monospace) — not the degraded plain-text path; html ->
  'content type "html" — web tier not wired up yet'.
- svg live-reload, real .d2 edit through the real router: 18182 -> 20888 bytes,
  viewBox re-read 936x366 -> 1307x401, token 0 -> 1 — exactly ONE bump, and no
  repeat bumps over 6 later polls. No window action taken.
- ws reconnect with backoff: daemon killed -> RECONNECT_SCHEDULED 1000, 2000,
  4000, 8000, 16000 with matching +1.0/+2.1/+4.1s retry gaps (cap 30000);
  client ALIVE, same window, process never exited on connection loss; after
  restart it re-attached and re-primed (FRAME path=sample.go type=code, set
  while disconnected) and the content actually rendered.
- Bad args: 5 bad forms (none / non-numeric N / missing port / non-numeric
  port / negative N) all -> rc=2 + 'usage: qml6 PreviewView.qml -- <slot-number>
  <port>' on stderr, 0 stack-trace markers.
- Async conversion COMPLETE: only 2 xhr.open() call sites in the file
  (:266, :489), neither passes a third arg; no literal 'false' third arg
  anywhere. No 'import QtWebEngine' / WebEngineView (T5's lazy tier not
  pre-broken); QtQuick.Layouts import gone.
- 9-value vocabulary consumed exactly: classifyPath emits {image, video, stl,
  svg, akm, md, html, code, none}; delegateFor handles image/svg/md/code/video
  + readable 'default:'; fallbackMessage handles html/akm/stl/none + 'default:'
  for unknown future strings.

GUARDS — TRIED TO DEFEAT ALL THREE, NONE BROKE:
- last-wins: forced out-of-order via per-path latency (a.d2 4s, b.d2 0.2s).
  a.d2's 18182-byte body landed while baseUrl was b.d2 -> LASTWINS_DISCARD;
  state stayed natW=356 natH=787 lastLen=16405 (b's document). Content never
  mixed across ~10 further polls.
- _pendingUrl anti-pile-up: 10 relay GETs during a 30s frame on a 3s relay
  (naive 1s poll would be ~30); POLL_SKIP_INFLIGHT observed firing repeatedly.
- _pendingUrl NO DEADLOCK (the freeze-forever risk): 502 error path clears it
  and polling resumes on the very next tick (8 consecutive 502s, each followed
  by a fresh POLL_SEND). A 60s upstream HANG cannot wedge it either, because
  preview-d's own 5s relay timeout always answers -> guard clears -> polling
  resumes, and live-reload then worked on recovery (18182 -> 18966, token 0->1).
- lastLen === -1 separation: initial response establishes natW/natH with NO
  bump; the first real change bumps exactly once; document switches (b->a)
  produce no spurious bump.

TESTS: no new automated tests — correct per the task's own test_plan ('QML has
no unit harness here — the repo precedent is BoardView'); verification is
scripted/manual, which both implementer and reviewer performed independently.
Existing Go suite unaffected and green on BOTH sides (sandbox disabled, per the
known /sbin/ffmpeg false alarm): base 'ok preview 4.223s', branch 'ok preview
4.372s'; go vet clean on both.

SCOPE: git diff main...HEAD touches preview/qml/PreviewView.qml only. Clean
merge into main (bc3b053) verified by merge-tree. No TODO/FIXME/stub/dead-code
hits.

DEVIATIONS: the implementer's honest 'could not reproduce the death' flag was
the crux of this audit and is now resolved in its favour — it was an
environment limitation (no ping-aware WM), not a weak fix.

ONE FINDING, non-blocking, filed as dotfiles-qyfj (P3): the comment at
:390-395 states a FALSE QML scoping rule — it claims a bare 'parent' inside the
non-visual Timer resolved to the Loader. Measured otherwise: bare 'parent'
resolves to the DELEGATE ITEM (the Timer's QObject parent) and read the Item's
property correctly, so the pre-fix code was NOT bound to the wrong object.
Corroborated: pre-fix issued 15 relay GETs in one 30s svg frame, which is only
possible if the Timer's 'parent.baseUrl' resolved correctly. 'id: svgTier' is a
real readability win but fixes a bug that never existed; zero functional
impact, so it does not gate the merge — but the false rule must not propagate
into the AKM graph at spec-retro. qyfj also records a bounded cosmetic
same-url concurrency window in poll() (one redundant repaint under rapid
a->b->a flapping; content never mixed, state converges).

T9 hand-off recorded on dotfiles-zw0d.9: re-verify svg-tier stability on ':10'
itself (confirmation, not an open gap — T4's evidence used a simulated
ping-aware WM), and record whether ':10's WM implements _NET_WM_PING, since
that turns any multi-second GUI block into a window-killing bug class.

design:

- `GET /api/svg?path=<abs>` returns the current compiled SVG bytes as
  `image/svg+xml` for a registered `.d2` path, lazy-spawning the child if
  needed — same 400-on-relative / 404-outside-registry semantics as
  `/api/resolve` ([[ft002]] api_surface parity), wrong method → 405 + Allow.
- The child spawn (`spawnLocked`) passes an explicit output path under
  `~/.cache/d2-router/svg/<project>/<basename>.svg` — previewing a `.d2` no
  longer writes an untracked sibling `.svg` into the repo (dotfiles-eq8;

Child compiled nothing yet (first hit races the initial compile) → bounded
retry/poll before 200, 503 after the deadline, never a hang. d2 compile
error → the route serves the last good svg if one exists, else 503 with the
child's lastError text. Verify the child still serves `/<basename>.svg`
when the output arg is an absolute path elsewhere — if it does not, the
router reads the cache-dir output file directly (fallback mechanism, same
contract). Cache dir missing → created on spawn. Path with spaces →
url-encoded query handled. Registry project removed while child runs →
404 on next fetch, child reaped normally.

Extend the fake-child helper suite: spawn-args test asserts the explicit
output path is present and repo-sibling write is gone (tmpdir project,
assert no `*.svg` beside the source). Route tests: registered path → 200 +

Parameterize on HOTKEYD_BIN + HOTKEYD_PROC_PAT, defaulting to the current python invocation so behaviour is unchanged. Suites must stay green against Python before anything else is dropped in.

Worth doing independently of sp021 (the Go rewrite): it is the only mechanism that can PROVE parity between two implementations rather than asserting it. Blocks the sp021 parallel-run strategy.

Note: the negative-validation stages inject a bad table at runtime via --binds ($TMP/faulty.py, $T8/trap.py). A suckless implementation with binds compiled in has no --binds flag, so those stages need a different shape — flag when doing the work, do not silently drop them.
