title: [bug] clip-sync wedges on blocking xclip -o (no timeout) — image selection owner hangs the loop
description: clip-sync.sh calls 'xclip -selection <sel> -o' with no timeout. Under xrdp/WSLg, if the selection owner is unresponsive (e.g. an image/bmp selection, or a dead xrdp client), xclip -o blocks indefinitely. One hung read freezes the whole poll loop -> PRIMARY<->CLIPBOARD sync stops -> paste serves stale content. Observed: daemon child 'xclip -selection clipboard -o' stuck 1m34s, a separate 'xclip -selection clipboard -t image/bmp -o' stuck 2h. Fix: wrap all xclip invocations in 'timeout' so a hung read/write is abandoned and the loop continues next tick. Follow-up to dotfiles-m1y / dotfiles-f3c.
close_reason: timeout-guarded all xclip calls; live-tested both directions, no wedge

title: [bug] clip-sync autostart pkill self-matches launcher — daemon never survives i3 reload
description: wsl.conf line 24 'pkill -f i3/scripts/clip-sync.sh; ~/.i3/scripts/clip-sync.sh &' runs via sh -c. The sh -c cmdline contains the substring 'i3/scripts/clip-sync.sh', so pkill -f matches its own parent shell + the just-launched child, killing clip-sync before it runs. Result: no PRIMARY<->CLIPBOARD sync in WSL/xrdp, only a stale orphan xclip -i. Regression in dotfiles-f3c (commit 88d862d). Fix: anchor pkill pattern with $ so it matches the running script cmdline (ends in clip-sync.sh) but not the launcher (ends in &).
close_reason: Anchored pkill pattern with $; live-tested bidirectional sync + reload leaves 1 daemon

title: bd git auto-hooks installed despite akm bd init — stale jsonl import clobbers closes during work-merge
description: Found during work-merge of dotfiles-ak8.1 (branch bd-dotfiles-ak8.1.1, merge 5f88717). /home/jan/.dotfiles/.git/hooks contains post-checkout and post-merge bd hooks. During land-bd-task.sh (git checkout main + git merge), the hooks re-imported the stale .beads jsonl snapshot and reverted dotfiles-ak8.1 from CLOSED back to OPEN/P2, wiping the audit-evidence close and the implementer notes. The close had to be re-applied manually. CLAUDE.md states 'bd auto-hooks are uninstalled by akm bd init' and config.yaml has no-auto-flush/no-auto-import — but the hooks are present, so something re-installed them (bd hooks install?). Fix: re-run akm bd init (idempotent per CLAUDE.md) and find what re-installs the hooks, or the clobber loop will eat every reviewer close that coincides with a git checkout/merge.
close_reason:
Remediated — verified 2026-07-20, no code change needed. The acute clobber cannot occur in the current state.

The bug (2026-06-12): active post-checkout/post-merge bd hooks ran bd import on every git checkout/merge, reloading the stale jsonl and reverting closed issues to open.

Current state, verified:
- Every bd hook in .git/hooks is an INERT worktree-guard stub — no bd import/export/hooks-run logic in any of them (grep-confirmed). post-checkout/post-merge do not exist as active hooks; bd hooks list reports both 'not installed'.
- akm bd doctor --diagnose: all green, incl. '✓ no auto-export/import hook logic', export.auto=false, dolt.auto-commit=on, snapshot in sync with Dolt.
- Ran akm bd init (the issue's own prescribed idempotent remedy) to re-assert: 'bd auto-hooks stripped, bd config pinned, Dolt schema healed'. Removed two dead post-*.disabled leftover files from .git/hooks.

Reinstaller identified (the issue's open question 'find what re-installs the hooks'): NOT anything in the dotfiles automation (grep of *.sh/*.nu/akm found no 'bd hooks install'). It is a MANUAL 'bd hooks install' — bd's own 'bd doctor' nags 'Missing 2 recommended hooks'. Verified in an isolated throwaway repo that bd 1.0.4's 'bd hooks install' writes hooks running 'bd hooks run post-merge/post-checkout' (clobber-capable; an explicit 'bd hooks run' is NOT stopped by the no-auto-import config guard).

Recurrence is self-defended: akm's bd_race_hooks regex 'bd +(export|import|hooks +run)' MATCHES a reinstalled 'bd hooks run' hook, so akm bd doctor detects + strips it, and CLAUDE.md documents 'run akm bd init after bd hooks install re-installs auto-hooks'. The akm hardening (bd_race_hooks treating inert worktree-gate stubs as harmless; bd_strip_hooks) clearly landed after this June-12 issue and is what produced the current safe state.

Durable hardening (core.hooksPath redirect to permanently defeat bd hooks install) was considered and declined as disproportionate: acute bug remediated, recurrence needs a manual mis-step against documented guidance, and akm bd doctor already auto-heals it. Filed nothing further.

title: focus-dim: quickshell dialogs stay bright with rest dimmed
description: Follow-up to dotfiles-0xd. When a quickshell dialog (run launcher, notifications, popups, etc.) is summoned (e.g. $mod+p), it should be treated as the focused cut-out (bright) with the rest of the screen dimmed. Currently quickshell + Rofi are in IGNORE_CLASSES which makes focus_rect=None and the entire screen dim. Switch behavior: detect quickshell-spawned dialogs and use their geometry as the focus_rect instead of ignoring them. Applies to both X11 (qs-focus-dim.py) and Wayland (FocusDimWayland.qml). Verify bar itself still stays bright (z-order distinguishes dialog from bar).
design:
# Focus-dim: Dialogs Stay Bright — Implementation Plan

> **For Claude:** Use infinifu:plan-scrum-master (automated) or infinifu:plan-supervised (user reviews each batch) to implement this plan.

**Goal:** When a focused window is a quickshell `qs-` popup, Rofi, or any floating window, the dim cut-out follows it (window bright, rest dimmed). When a non-floating ignored class (the quickshell bar) is "focused", or there is no focus, the screen fully dims. Behavior identical on X11/i3 and Wayland/sway.

**Bd epic:** `dotfiles-56r`

**Predecessor:** `dotfiles-0xd` (focus-dim base, merged).

**Architecture:** Extend the existing focus-decision logic in two files (`quickshell/qs-focus-dim.py`, `quickshell/config/FocusDimWayland.qml`). Add a "is floating" signal to the focus walker so floating windows bypass the class-based ignore. Remove `rofi` from the ignore list. Invert the `qs-` title branch from ignore to focus-target.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3 + GTK3 + cairo (X11), Quickshell QML + `swaymsg` (Wayland). No new dependencies.

---

## Conventions

- Quickshell config in `quickshell/config/` (symlinked via rotz). Helper scripts in `quickshell/`.
- Verification is **manual visual confirmation** — no automated overlay test framework. Synthetic tree-walk tests for the Python `walk` / `should_ignore` are allowed and encouraged (the dotfiles-0xd T3 implementer used them).
- Commits use Conventional Commits: `feat(quickshell):`, `fix(quickshell):`, `refactor(quickshell):`.
- Anti-patterns inherited from dotfiles-0xd remain in force (see `board/done/focus-dim.md` once archived, otherwise `board/ready/focus-dim.md`):
  - No silent exception swallow — `print(..., file=sys.stderr, flush=True)` in `except` paths.
  - No Xlib at module top-level.
  - No `--no-verify` on commits. Pre-commit hooks must pass.
  - No TODO without follow-up bd task.
  - Do not introduce a new dispatch path or new files — modify in place.

## File tree (changes only)

```
quickshell/
├── qs-focus-dim.py            (modified — walker + should_ignore)
└── config/
    └── FocusDimWayland.qml    (modified — applyContainer + walker)
```

## Task 1: X11 — floating + qs- titled treated as focusable, rofi removed

Update the Python overlay so floating windows and `qs-` titled windows become cut-out targets. Remove `Rofi`/`rofi` from `IGNORE_CLASSES`.

**Files:**
- Modify: `quickshell/qs-focus-dim.py`
- Create: `quickshell/test_qs_focus_dim_dialogs.py` (one-shot synthetic walk test)

**Step 1: Write the failing synthetic walk test**

The codebase has no test harness, but `qs-focus-dim.py` is plain Python — we can drive `walk` + `should_ignore` directly. Create `quickshell/test_qs_focus_dim_dialogs.py`:

```python
"""One-shot synthetic walk tests for qs-focus-dim dialog handling.
Run: python3 quickshell/test_qs_focus_dim_dialogs.py
"""
import importlib.util, pathlib, sys, types

# Stub gi/cairo before import so the GTK overlay code doesn't try to draw.
sys.modules.setdefault("gi", type(sys)("gi"))
sys.modules["gi"].require_version = lambda *a, **k: None
gi_repo = types.ModuleType("gi.repository")
for n in ("Gtk", "Gdk", "GLib"):
    setattr(gi_repo, n, types.SimpleNamespace())
sys.modules["gi.repository"] = gi_repo
sys.modules["cairo"] = types.SimpleNamespace()

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "qsd", pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "qs-focus-dim.py"
)
qsd = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(qsd)


def make_leaf(cls="", title="", fullscreen=0):
    return {
        "focused": True,
        "window": 1,
        "window_properties": {"class": cls, "instance": cls},
        "name": title,
        "rect": {"x": 100, "y": 100, "width": 800, "height": 600},
        "deco_rect": {"height": 0},
        "fullscreen_mode": fullscreen,
        "nodes": [],
        "floating_nodes": [],
    }


def wrap_floating(leaf):
    return {"nodes": [], "floating_nodes": [
        {"nodes": [leaf], "floating_nodes": []}
    ]}


def wrap_tiled(leaf):
    return {"nodes": [leaf], "floating_nodes": []}


def run():
    # Case 1: regular tiled window — focusable
    qsd.focus_rect = None
    qsd._compute_focus_rect(wrap_tiled(make_leaf(cls="Firefox", title="example.com - Mozilla Firefox")))
    assert qsd.focus_rect is not None, "regular tiled window should produce focus_rect"

    # Case 2: floating qs- dialog — focusable
    qsd.focus_rect = None
    qsd._compute_focus_rect(wrap_floating(make_leaf(cls="quickshell", title="qs-overlay-projects")))
    assert qsd.focus_rect is not None, "floating qs- dialog must be focusable"

    # Case 3: floating Rofi — focusable (rofi removed from IGNORE_CLASSES)
    qsd.focus_rect = None
    qsd._compute_focus_rect(wrap_floating(make_leaf(cls="Rofi", title="rofi")))
    assert qsd.focus_rect is not None, "floating rofi must be focusable now"

    # Case 4: bar (class quickshell, tiled, no qs- title) — IGNORED
    qsd.focus_rect = "PLACEHOLDER"
    qsd._compute_focus_rect(wrap_tiled(make_leaf(cls="quickshell", title="")))
    assert qsd.focus_rect is None, "tiled quickshell bar must remain ignored"

    # Case 5: qs- titled tiled window — focusable via title prefix
    qsd.focus_rect = None
    qsd._compute_focus_rect(wrap_tiled(make_leaf(cls="anything", title="qs-anything")))
    assert qsd.focus_rect is not None, "qs- titled tiled window should be focusable"

    # Case 6: fullscreen wins over focusable
    qsd.focus_rect = "PLACEHOLDER"
    qsd._compute_focus_rect(wrap_floating(make_leaf(cls="quickshell", title="qs-foo", fullscreen=1)))
    assert qsd.focus_rect is None, "fullscreen wins over focusable"

    # Case 7: no focused window — full dim
    qsd.focus_rect = "PLACEHOLDER"
    qsd._compute_focus_rect({"nodes": [], "floating_nodes": []})
    assert qsd.focus_rect is None, "no focus → full dim"

    print("All 7 synthetic walk cases passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()
```

**Step 3: Refactor `qs-focus-dim.py` to apply the new rule + expose a pure decision helper**

In `quickshell/qs-focus-dim.py`:

1. Change `IGNORE_CLASSES`:
   ```python

   ```

2. Update `should_ignore` to take `in_floating`:
   ```python
   def should_ignore(c, in_floating):
       """Return True if c should be treated as 'no focused window' (full dim)."""
       if in_floating:
           return False
       props = c.get('window_properties', {})
       cls = props.get('class', '')
       instance = props.get('instance', '')
       title = c.get('name', '')
       if title.startswith('qs-'):
           return False
       return cls in IGNORE_CLASSES or instance in IGNORE_CLASSES
   ```

3. Update `walk` to track floating-subtree descent:
   ```python
   def walk(node, parents, in_floating):
       if node.get('focused') and node.get('window'):
           return node, parents, in_floating
       for child in node.get('nodes', []):
           r = walk(child, parents + [node], in_floating)
           if r:
               return r
       for child in node.get('floating_nodes', []):
           r = walk(child, parents + [node], True)
           if r:
               return r
       return None
   ```

4. Extract the decision logic into a pure `_compute_focus_rect(tree)` at module scope so the test can call it without GTK:
   ```python
   def _compute_focus_rect(tree):
       """Update module-level focus_rect from an i3 tree dict. Pure function (no GTK)."""
       global focus_rect
       result = walk(tree, [], False)
       if not result:
           focus_rect = None
           return
       leaf, parents, in_floating = result
       if should_ignore(leaf, in_floating) or leaf.get('fullscreen_mode', 0) > 0:
           focus_rect = None
           return
       r = leaf.get('rect', {})
       deco_h = leaf.get('deco_rect', {}).get('height', 0)
       in_tabbed = any(p.get('layout') in ('tabbed', 'stacked') for p in parents)
       direct_in_tabbed = parents and parents[-1].get('layout') in ('tabbed', 'stacked')
       if in_tabbed and not direct_in_tabbed:
           deco_h = 0
       focus_rect = (
           r.get('x', 0),
           r.get('y', 0) - deco_h,
           r.get('width', 0),
           r.get('height', 0) + deco_h,
       )
   ```

5. Replace `refresh_focused._do` body so it calls `_compute_focus_rect`:

   ```python
   def refresh_focused():

               tree = json.loads(
                   subprocess.check_output(
   ```

The previous inline `walk` and inline decision logic (the entire `if not result: ... else: ...` block currently in `refresh_focused._do`) are now removed — replaced by the single call to `_compute_focus_rect(tree)`. Don't leave the old code around as a fallback.

## Task 2: Wayland — floating + qs- titled treated as focusable, rofi removed

Mirror Task 1 in `FocusDimWayland.qml`. Sway represents floating windows in their workspace's `floating_nodes` array; the walker needs to track that descent.

**Files:**
- Modify: `quickshell/config/FocusDimWayland.qml`

**Step 1: Verify sway floating tree shape (~5 minutes, before editing)**

Canonical sway tree shape (verified against sway IPC docs):

- Workspace nodes contain `nodes` (tiled children) and `floating_nodes` (floating children).
- A node inside `floating_nodes` typically has `type: "floating_con"` and either represents the window directly or contains it as a `con` child.
- Leaf con: `type: "con"`, with `app_id` (Wayland-native), `window_properties.class` (XWayland), and a `pid`.

The walker marks `in_floating = true` when descending into `floating_nodes`. This is the same propagation strategy as the i3 Python path (Task 1) — keeps logic symmetric.

If a live sway session is available, sanity-check with:
```bash
swaymsg -t get_tree | jq '.. | select(.type? == "floating_con") | {name, app_id, type}' | head
```
Expected: at least one entry per visible floating window. If unavailable, proceed using the documented shape — the synthetic guarantee is "anything reachable only via `floating_nodes` is in_floating".

**Step 2: Modify `applyContainer` to accept `in_floating`**

Current signature (line 202): `function applyContainer(c) { ... }`. Update to:

```qml
readonly property var ignoreAppIds: ["quickshell"]  // rofi removed

function applyContainer(c, in_floating) {
    var appId = c.app_id || ""
    var cls = (c.window_properties || {}).class || ""
    var title = c.name || ""

    if (c.fullscreen_mode > 0) {
        hasFocus = false
        return
    }
    // Floating windows and qs- titled windows bypass class-based ignore
    if (!in_floating && !title.startsWith("qs-")) {
        if (ignoreAppIds.indexOf(appId) >= 0 || ignoreAppIds.indexOf(cls) >= 0) {
            hasFocus = false
            return
        }
    }
    var r = c.rect || {}
    var decoH = (c.deco_rect || {}).height || 0
    fx = r.x || 0
    fy = (r.y || 0) - decoH
    fw = r.width || 0
    fh = (r.height || 0) + decoH
    hasFocus = (fw > 0 && fh > 0)
}
```

Control-flow order matters: fullscreen first (always wins), then the floating/qs- bypass, then the class-ignore check.

**Step 3: Update `focusScan.onExited` walker to track `in_floating`**

Current walker body (lines 183–194):
```qml
function walk(node) {
    if (found) return
    if (node.focused && node.pid) {
        dimOverlay.applyContainer(node)
        found = true
        return
    }
    var children = (node.nodes || []).concat(node.floating_nodes || [])
    for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) walk(children[i])
}
walk(tree)
```

Replace with:
```qml
function walk(node, in_floating) {
    if (found) return
    if (node.focused && node.pid) {
        dimOverlay.applyContainer(node, in_floating)
        found = true
        return
    }
    var tiled = node.nodes || []
    for (var i = 0; i < tiled.length; i++) walk(tiled[i], in_floating)
    var floating = node.floating_nodes || []
    for (var j = 0; j < floating.length; j++) walk(floating[j], true)
}
walk(tree, false)
```

**Step 4: Update the event-driven call sites (`swaySubscribe`)**

The event-driven path (`swaySubscribe.onRead` handlers around lines 94 and 97) currently calls `applyContainer(e.container)` directly. The single-container event payload does not include parent-walk info, so the safest fix is to trigger a fresh `focusScan` instead of calling `applyContainer` directly.

For each `dimOverlay.applyContainer(e.container)` call inside `swaySubscribe.onRead`, replace with:
```qml
focusScan.running = true
```

Rationale: `focusScan` walks the whole tree with `in_floating` propagation, so the floating state is always correct. The cost is one extra `swaymsg -t get_tree` per event, which is the same cost the i3 path already pays via the always-`get_tree` `refresh_focused`. Performance is acceptable for human-scale focus events.

Also add a subscription to the `floating` window event so toggling tiled↔floating updates the overlay. Inside `swaySubscribe`'s parsed-event branches, add `else if (e.change === "floating")` that also triggers `focusScan.running = true`.

**Step 5: Mechanical syntax check + grep regression checks**

Without a live sway session, agents cannot start quickshell. Run these greps in the worktree:

```bash

# Expected exactly one hit, content: ["quickshell"]  (no "rofi")
```

title: wm-state: restore must defer old-terminal kill until new attach
design:
## Bug
pre-clean-target kills target ws's terminals BEFORE the new respawn-flow attaches new kittys. Killing the kitty detaches its tmux client. tmux-start sets destroy-unattached on, plus tmux-cleanup hook fires on client-detached and kills any unattached non-pinned sessions in the group. Result: by the time main restore issues exec kitty -e tmux attach -t <session>, the session is gone and the new kitty's tmux attach fails. Saved tmux_window_id worthless.

## Reproducer
1. wm-state save with 3 kittys, each in its own tmux session (local_3..5).
2. wm-state restore <same ws>.
3. pre-clean-target kills the 3 kittys -> their tmux clients detach -> destroy-unattached + cleanup hook destroy local_3..5.
4. exec kitty -e tmux attach -t local_3 fails (no such session).

## Fix
Split pre-clean into two phases:
- isolate-target <name>: rename target -> <name>-old, no kill. Old terminals stay alive on <name>-old, tmux clients stay attached, sessions stay alive.
- kill-old-terminals <name>-old: walk -old ws, kill terminal windows. Run AFTER new respawn finished and new kittys attached to those sessions (so each session has the new client, destroy-unattached doesn't fire).

main restore loop:
  1. for ws: isolate-target (rename only)
  2. for ws: workspace + append_layout + exec new terminals
  3. wait for new windows mapped+swallowed (poll i3 tree, or sleep ~500ms)
  4. for ws: kill-old-terminals on <name>-old
  5. return to start_ws

Collision case (<name>-old already exists from prior restore): handle in isolate-target the same way pre-clean-target does today (kill its terminals first since those are leftover from a previous run; then rename current target on top).

## Why bug not feature
Current code kills sessions before reattach -> happy path is broken end-to-end. Smoke scenarios 1-3 in ciw.6 only passed because the implementer attached new kittys to fresh wmsmoke_a/b/c sessions they created manually, not to the saved ones. Real-world restore against grouped local_N sessions fails.

## Acceptance
- [ ] After wm-state restore, every saved tmux session is still alive (verify tmux list-sessions before+after).
- [ ] Each new kitty's tmux client is attached to the originally-saved session (verify via tmux display-message -p '#{window_id}').
- [ ] Old terminals on <name>-old are killed by end of restore.
- [ ] -old workspace contains only non-terminal leftovers (firefox etc.) after restore completes.

## Out of scope
Polling for swallow completion (could be added later); MVP can use a fixed delay after spawn loop.
close_reason: Split pre-clean into isolate-target (rename only) + kill-old-terminals (run after spawn). Restore now: rename target -> -old (phase 1), focus + append_layout + exec new attaches (per ws), sleep 600ms, kill old terminals on -old (phase 2), return to start_ws. Old tmux sessions stay alive across the cutover because their old client survives until the new client has attached.

title: test precision: the draws assertions in test_qs_focus_border_mode.py do not pin _set_layer_state's explicit queue_draw
description:
Found during work-audit of dotfiles-0tv1.2 (sp024 Task 2). Non-blocking: production code is correct, the task shipped approved.

GAP. quickshell/test_qs_focus_border_mode.py added a separate draws recorder (FakeWin.queue_draw) to prove constraint 2 - that _set_layer_state carries the deleted i3-mode branch refresh_focused + queue_draw pair. The refresh half IS pinned. The queue_draw half is NOT: Border.update() at quickshell/qs-focus-border.py:188 ends with self.win.queue_draw(), so any refresh that reaches apply_geom populates draws on its own. The three positive assertions (aiming-enter: queues an explicit redraw for the colour flip; aiming-clear: queues an explicit redraw; handoff: the clear queues a redraw) therefore add nothing over the adjacent show in calls assertion.

MUTATION EVIDENCE (audit, scratchpad copy, production file untouched):
- drop refresh_focused() from _set_layer_state  -> 9 FAIL, incl. both aiming refresh cases. Discriminating.
- drop border.win.queue_draw() from _set_layer_state -> 83 PASS, 0 FAIL, exit 0. NOT discriminating.

The explicit queue_draw is genuinely load-bearing in production: refresh_focused is async and bails on _refresh_lock contention, on mode_suppressed, and on _has_overlay_present, in which cases the synchronous queue_draw is the only repaint.

Also note the rationale comment ("refresh_focused skips the GTK draw when the geometry is identical") is inaccurate - there is no geometry-comparison short-circuit anywhere in qs-focus-border.py. It is INHERITED verbatim from main (lines 328 and 468 pre-cutover), not introduced by Task 2.

FIX DIRECTION. Make the positive draws assertions discriminate - e.g. clear draws AFTER the refresh settles, or count draws vs the refresh path, or assert the pair under a stubbed refresh_focused that does not reach border.update. Then correct the rationale comment to name the real reason (async refresh may bail; the synchronous draw is the guarantee) rather than a geometry short-circuit that does not exist.

The negative uses of draws (a repeat of the same layer state does not redraw; a stale i3 mode event cannot redraw over a live layer) are sound and should be kept as-is.

Natural home: dotfiles-0tv1.3 (suite coverage) or a standalone follow-up.
close_reason: Fixed. explicit_draws_from() isolates the explicit queue_draw by stubbing refresh_focused, removing Border.update()'s competing draw. Mutation-verified: deleting border.win.queue_draw from _set_layer_state now fails all three isolated assertions, where it previously passed 83/0. Inaccurate geometry-short-circuit rationale corrected in both the test and the production comment. Suite 83/0; test-mode-bar 119/0; test-screenshot-launcher 3/0.

title: test-hotkeyd.sh stage 15 fails on dev boxes with a real leftover panic fallback link in $HOME/.i3/config.d
design: Observed while verifying dotfiles-ugdg: running test-hotkeyd.sh (any engine) on a dev machine that has previously run hotkeyd-panic.sh panic for real leaves /home/<user>/.i3/config.d/zz-fallback-binds.conf symlinked to the repo's i3/config.d/zz-fallback-binds.conf. Stage 15 ('missing grabs report DEGRADED') does not override HOME the way stages 8/10 do (grep test-hotkeyd.sh for HOME="$T8"/"$C10" — those sandbox it, stage 15 does not), so it reads the REAL i3 config.d and sees CONTESTED instead of DEGRADED, producing 6 failures unrelated to any code or doc change. Fix: sandbox HOME for stage 15 the same way stages 8/10 do, OR document that test-hotkeyd.sh (unlike test-panic.sh/test-launcher.sh) is not HOME-safe and must not be run on a box with a real hotkeyd panic history without first clearing ~/.i3/config.d/zz-fallback-binds.conf. Repro: on a box where ~/.i3/config.d/zz-fallback-binds.conf is linked, run HOTKEYD_ENGINE_DEFAULT=go HOTKEYD_BIN=./hotkeyd HOTKEYD_PROC_PAT=hotkeyd HOTKEYD_HAS_BINDS_FLAG=0 bash test-hotkeyd.sh -> stage 15 shows CONTESTED FAILs referencing the real ~/.i3/config.d path.
close_reason: DUPLICATE of dotfiles-vg16 (opened 2026-07-30, predates this one, filed from dotfiles-2ats verification). Both describe the exact same bug: hotkeyd/test-hotkeyd.sh stage 15 ('missing grabs report DEGRADED') calls hotkeyd.sh status without sandboxing HOME/HOTKEYD_I3_CONFIG_D the way stages 8/10 do, so on a machine with a real ~/.i3/config.d/zz-fallback-binds.conf panic-fallback symlink it reads real state and reports CONTESTED instead of DEGRADED -- 6 false failures unrelated to any code change. vg16 has the fuller root-cause writeup (identifies the exact stage-8 sandboxing pattern to replicate: HOME="$T8" HOTKEYD_I3_CONFIG_D="$T8/config.d") and reproduced it against both pre- and post-dotfiles-2ats trees, confirming it's pre-existing. Consolidating tracking onto vg16; no unique information in pcmc is lost (same repro, same fix direction).

title: livecheck: grab-report settle identifies A publication, not THE layer's
description:
Found by the 3rd audit of dotfiles-ylmp.13 (cmd/livecheck).

daemonchecks.go:553-559 'and the layer\'s grabs cost zero refusals' is gated on
openLanded = grabWatch.settled(), which proves that A grab report was published
after the baseline but NOT that it is the one describing the layer just entered.

REPRODUCER (observer-side, no daemon change needed to see it):
  add `time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)` at the head of publishGrabReport in
  hotkeyd/cmd/hotkeyd/daemon.go:612, build, and run cmd/livecheck against it on an
  isolated Xvfb + i3. 500 ms is inside the python-sync envelope settle.go:84-85
  documents, so this models a slower engine, not a broken one.

OBSERVED (twice, and identical for 4b53e447 and 8335b6c7):
  livecheck: 80 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip
  PASS $mod+Tab opens the switcher and takes the layer
  PASS and the layer\'s grabs cost zero refusals -- wanted=70 active=70 missing=[]
  PASS $mod+Escape was actually GRABBED, not merely requested
  PASS q was actually GRABBED, not merely requested
The switcher layer (87 chords) was open and its own chords were demonstrably
grabbed, while the line graded the DEFAULT layer\'s 70-chord report. Healthy runs
print 87/87 there.

ROOT CAUSE: when a publication from the PREVIOUS transition is still in flight at
the moment watchGrabs() takes its baseline (daemonchecks.go:493), that in-flight
write satisfies settled(), and the read at daemonchecks.go:557 returns the previous
layer\'s report. openLanded buys latency, not identification. Same class as the
signal settle.go:28-34 already rejected once.

NOT the settled GAP-1 finding: that established the stamp never MISSES a
publication. This is a different property -- the settled publication is not shown
to BELONG to the layer under test.

SEVERITY: cannot green a broken daemon; it grades a real, correct report belonging
to the wrong layer, so the claim is weaker than advertised rather than false. Both
real engines grade 87/87 correctly today.

FIX DIRECTION (observer-only, adr0018-safe): grabWatch already captures the
pre-transition report body in w.base.body (settle.go:104,134). Expose it and require
the graded report to differ from the pre-transition baseline, or assert the wanted
count against the switcher layer\'s own expected size, so a still-previous report
SKIPs. Verify by re-running the 500 ms fault and showing SKIP (or 87) where it now
PASSes at 70.

Applies to the sibling report claim at daemonchecks.go:51 only for the default layer
(no prior transition), which is why that one is unaffected.
notes:
FIXED on bd-dotfiles-ylmp.13.0 @ 5824561e (4th-round escalation). Observer-only; production diff still 0 lines.

DEVIATION FROM THE PRESCRIBED FIX, with evidence.
The writeup prescribed 'expose w.base.body and require the graded report to differ from that baseline'. MEASURED: that does not discriminate. Instrumented the faulted run and printed the three values at daemonchecks.go:557 --
  INSTRUMENT switcher: base={"pid":2078661,"wanted":106,"active":105,"missing":["Meta_R"]} graded=wanted=70 active=70 missing=[] openLanded=true
The baseline is NAV's report (106), two transitions back -- under publish lag the section-start reading is ITSELF stale -- while the graded one is DEFAULT's (70). They differ, so 'graded != baseline' passes and the defect survives. The prescription's INTENT (graded must not be the pre-transition report) is right; its chosen bytes are not the pre-transition layer's.

WHAT SHIPPED
- settle.go: grabWatch.baselineSet() (parsed pre-input reading, per the prescription) + sameGrabSet() (compares what a report SAYS, not the publication -- the exact inverse of settled()'s question, and both are needed).
- daemonchecks.go: notAPriorReport(cur, have, priors...) gate. Refuses any grab set this run had ALREADY read before the transition. Two priors at the switcher site: (1) the DEFAULT layer's report read at daemonchecks.go:47, threaded in; (2) openWatch.baselineSet(). Both, because of the finding above.
- A MISSING report deliberately still FAILs (gate holds when have==false) -- that is the daemon's failure, not a precondition gap. Behaviour there unchanged.

PROOF (500 ms sleep at head of publishGrabReport / write_grab_report; fault lived only in scratchpad copies, repo byte-identical after, git status clean)
  GO   before: PASS and the layer's grabs cost zero refusals - wanted=70 active=70 missing=[]   | 80 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip
  GO   after:  SKIP and the layer's grabs cost zero refusals - CANNOT JUDGE - the report graded here (wanted=70 active=70 missing=[]) is the SAME grab set as the DEFAULT layer's report, read at the start of this daemon phase, so it is a publication about the PREVIOUS layer that landed late   | 79 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip
  (reproduced twice, displays :47 and :52)
  PY   before: PASS ... wanted=70 ... | 80/0/0     PY after: SKIP (same reason) | 79/0/1
  The python arm shows the defect was never Go-specific and the cure is engine-neutral.

NO REGRESSION: healthy 80 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip on BOTH engines, before and after, switcher line PASSing at wanted=87 active=87 as it should.

Unit tests added (settle_test.go, observe_test.go): settled()-does-not-identify (stages the exact nav-baseline/default-landing shape), baselineSet, sameGrabSet, and the gate's four branches incl. 'no report still FAILs' and 'an unread prior rules nothing out'.
close_reason:
AUDITED: FIXED and VERIFIED by the 4th audit of dotfiles-ylmp.13 (commit 5824561e, branch bd-dotfiles-ylmp.13.0).

Reviewer reproduced the defect and the cure independently, on private Xvfb + real i3 (:53-:61; live :10.0 untouched), with a 500ms sleep at the head of publishGrabReport / write_grab_report:
  GO  before (livecheck @8335b6c7): PASS 'and the layer's grabs cost zero refusals - wanted=70 active=70 missing=[]'  | 80 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip
  GO  after  (livecheck @5824561e): SKIP ... CANNOT JUDGE - the report graded here (wanted=70 active=70 missing=[]) is the SAME grab set as the DEFAULT layer's report, read at the start of this daemon phase ...  | 79 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip
  PY  before: PASS@70, 80/0/0     PY after: SKIP, 79/0/1
  HEALTHY both engines after the fix: 80/0/0, switcher line PASS at wanted=87 active=87.

THE FIX DIRECTION IN THIS BUG'S OWN NOTE WAS WRONG AND THE DEVIATION IS SOUND. This note prescribed 'expose w.base.body and require the graded report to differ from that baseline'. Reviewer instrumented daemonchecks.go:639 under the fault:
  base.body={"pid":2101641,"wanted":106,"active":105,"missing":["Meta_R"]}  graded=wanted=70  openLanded=true  PRESCRIPTION(graded != base.body)=TRUE
The section-start baseline is NAV's report from two transitions back, so the prescribed comparison passes and the defect survives untouched. Shipped instead: notAPriorReport(cur, have, priors...) refusing any grab set this run had already read before the transition, with BOTH pre-transition readings threaded (the default layer's report from daemonchecks.go:47 and openWatch.baselineSet()). That is the minimum that discriminates.

A missing report deliberately still FAILs (gate holds when have==false) - the daemon's failure, unchanged.

Residual noted for the record, not reproducible: a deeper publication backlog in which nav's 106-chord report lands late against a 70-chord baseline would slip past both priors. Reviewer measured the daemon's whole publication inventory for a run ({70 default, 106 nav, 87 switcher}) and tried to force it at 1500ms (3x the fault) - the shape did not change, because each settled() drains one publication. Would grade a real report of the wrong layer, never green a broken daemon.

title: sp022: qt6-websockets dependency is undeclared — fresh clone cannot run PreviewView.qml
description:
Found during sp022 T4 dispatch pre-flight (plan-scrum-master, 2026-07-30).

T4's PreviewView.qml requires the QtWebSockets QML module, but qt6-websockets is not installed on this machine and NOTHING in the repo declares it: no dot.yaml lists it, and grep for QtWebSockets across *.qml/*.yaml returns nothing. The sp022 design assigns 'dependency declaration' to T5, but scoped to the qt6-webengine web tier only — the websockets dep for the native ws client is unowned scope across the whole spec.

Present on this box: qt6-declarative, qt6-svg, qt6-webengine, /sbin/qml6. Missing: qt6-websockets.

Fix: declare qt6-websockets alongside whichever dot.yaml ends up owning the preview QML client (likely preview/dot.yaml or the quickshell/meta package that installs the runtime), so 'rotz install' on a fresh clone yields a working preview window. Verify by checking the QML import resolves: qml6 with an import QtWebSockets statement.

Blocks a clean fresh-clone install path, not T4 itself (T4 unblocked by a manual install).
close_reason: Closed by sp022 T5 (dotfiles-zw0d.5, merge 0efcece): preview/dot.yaml now declares both qt6-webengine and qt6-websockets behind a pacman --needed guard. All three guard branches (libs-present no-op, pacman-present install, no-pacman actionable message) independently verified in isolated PATH sandboxes by the T5 audit. A fresh clone will no longer hit the missing-QtWebSockets wall that blocked T4's dispatch mid-sprint.

title: focus border draws 24px too high on a leaf whose title is inside its own rect
description:
apply_geom in quickshell/qs-focus-border.py unconditionally does y = rect.y - deco_h, suppressing it only for a leaf nested in a tabbed ancestor.

Where the title bar sits relative to rect is NOT constant, and i3 reports it in window_rect.y (client offset inside rect):
  window_rect.y == 0       title drawn ABOVE rect (tab strip owned by parent) -> rect MUST be extended up
  window_rect.y == deco_h  title already INSIDE rect (leaf in a plain split)  -> extending up overshoots

Live evidence, workspace copacks, win 48234501 (lazygit, leaf directly in splith, no tabbed ancestor):
  rect        x=1282 y=33  w=1272 h=1401
  deco_rect   height=24
  window_rect y=24
  computed    x=1282 y=9   w=1272 h=1425   <- 24px too high, 24px too tall
  overlay window 16777219 measured at 1280,7 1276x1429 (computed + 2px outset) -> confirms

Tabbed siblings in the same workspace have window_rect.y=0 and are drawn correctly, which is why the bug only shows on windows that are NOT in a tabbed container.
close_reason:
Fixed in 6a67420. apply_geom now keys the upward extension off window_rect.y (client offset inside rect) instead of assuming rect always excludes the title bar.

Verified live on DISPLAY=:10 with the helper restarted:
  plain-split leaf (lazygit 48234501, frame 1282,33 1272x1401)
    before: overlay 1280,7  1276x1429  (24px high, 24px long)
    after:  overlay 1280,31 1276x1405  (exact)
  tabbed leaf (44040197, frame 6,33 1272x1401)
    after:  overlay 4,31 1276x1405  (unchanged, no regression)

New suite quickshell/test_qs_focus_border_geom.py pins all four shapes, was 3-red on the plain-split case before the fix. All 4 quickshell python suites pass.

title: Drop $mod+Shift+o (rename workspace) and $mod+Ctrl+x (xkill) outright
description:
USER DECISION, 2026-07-29: both deleted rather than migrated. Neither goes to binds.py, neither goes to the panic fallback — a panic must not resurrect a bind that was removed on purpose.

$mod+Shift+o — 'i3-input -F "name workspace to %s"'. sp019 had relocated it here from $mod+Shift+n to free that key for the notification picker. Workspaces in this setup are named by the project registry and reached POSITIONALLY (ws-switch.nu, the $mod+<n> row) or through the quickshell projects picker, so an ad-hoc rename prompt named a workspace the number row would then address by position anyway. 'i3-msg rename workspace to "x"' remains for the rare case.

$mod+Ctrl+x — xkill. Grabs the pointer, severs the X connection of whatever is clicked; kills the CLIENT, so a well-behaved app exits and a detached one lives on windowless. It was the escalation for a window ignoring $mod+Shift+q.

DECIDED AGAINST THE RECOMMENDATION on xkill, recorded because the reasoning should survive the decision: by the repo's own rule (config.common, above the kill bind) a key for dealing with something already misbehaving belongs in i3, which would have made it a fifth permanent recovery key. The counter-argument that won: pkill/kill -9 from any terminal does the same job with an accurate target, and a crosshair that destroys whatever it touches sits one modifier away from $mod+Ctrl+m.

TEST FALLOUT, both of the same shape as the parser-floor repoint earlier today — a pin whose VEHICLE had an expiry date:
- test-notif-history.sh's shift-o-is-name-workspace scenario asserted the bind exists on both entry points. INVERT rather than delete: sp019 needs $mod+Shift+n staying free pinned, and a deletion that took the coverage with it would leave nothing watching that.
- its MUTANT PIN used that same line as the vehicle for proving the include mechanism. Repoint at $mod+Shift+q, which is i3's by ARGUMENT and cannot expire.
close_reason:
DONE, commit 857743fb. Self-verified.

Both chords deleted from i3/config.common. Neither added to binds.py, neither
added to zz-fallback-binds.conf — asserted, not just intended.

LIVE on :10 after reload + daemon restart: $mod+Shift+o opened no i3-input
prompt (i3-input window set unchanged); $mod+Ctrl+x started no xkill (pgrep -c
xkill 0 -> 0, safe to press precisely because it is gone).

TEST FALLOUT handled rather than deleted:
- shift-o-is-name-workspace INVERTED: now asserts the bind is gone from both
  entry points, from the fallback and from binds.py. sp019's real requirement
  ($mod+Shift+n stays free for the notification picker) keeps a watcher.
- the MUTANT PIN that used the rename line as its vehicle would have gone
  vacuously green against a line no file contains. Repointed at $mod+Shift+q,
  which is i3's by argument and cannot expire.

XKILL WAS DROPPED AGAINST THE RECOMMENDATION — recorded so the reasoning
survives: the repo's own rule (config.common, above the kill bind) would have
made it a fifth permanent recovery key. If a window ever ignores $mod+Shift+q,
the answer is now pkill/kill -9 from a terminal.

title: Resize mode cutover: $mod+r and mode "resize" become a hotkeyd layer
description:
The last i3 MODE that is a keybind group. $mod+r plus the whole mode "resize" block (h/j/k/l at 5px, arrows at 10px, Return/Escape/q to leave) becomes LAYERS['resize'], the same treatment nav (dotfiles-hwds.16) and the system mode (dotfiles-hwds.38) got.

KEPT, NOT FOLDED INTO nav's Alt SUBLAYER, which also resizes: this one is a MODE — you enter it, both hands are free, it persists until you leave. nav's sublayer is for a correction made in passing while $mod is already held. Same verbs, different gesture; i3 carried both for the same reason.

THE 5/10 SPLIT IS THE PART A REWRITE WOULD LOSE. i3's mode moved letters by 5 and arrows by 10 — a coarse/fine pair on one gesture. nav's sublayer only ever had the 5, so reusing _nav_binds('resize') would silently halve the arrows.

THE BAR NEEDS NOTHING: naming the layer 'resize' means ModeBarTheme.resolve maps it to the same hints['resize'] row the i3 mode triggered, now fed from the state socket.
acceptance_criteria:
1. binds.py has LAYERS['resize'] + Bind($mod+r); config.common has neither the chord nor the block.
2. The fallback carries the chord AND the whole mode block verbatim, 5/10 split intact.
3. Stub keymap gains r; the layer's own keys came free from nav.
4. Bar paints the resize hint strip from the daemon's layer, unchanged registry.
5. Suites green; i3 -C clean on both entry points.
6. LIVE: $mod+r enters, bare h shrinks, a bare arrow grows by twice as much, Escape leaves — measured from i3's tree, not the daemon log.
close_reason:
DONE, commit 857743fb. Self-verified.

RED first: adding LAYERS['resize'] + $mod+r while i3 still had the mode ->
test_no_chord_is_owned_by_both_i3_and_the_daemon failed under Mod4 and Mod1.

CRITERIA: binds.py has the layer and the entry chord; config.common has neither
the chord nor the block; the fallback carries both verbatim with the 5/10 split
intact; stub keymap gains r (27); the bar needed NO change (the layer is named
'resize', so ModeBarTheme.resolve reaches the existing hints row); 71 -> 72
grabs on both displays; pytest 399/0, test-hotkeyd.sh 132/0, test-panic.sh
54/0, test-mode-bar.sh 111/0, nav both shapes, i3 -C clean.

LIVE on :10, read from i3's TREE not the daemon log: $mod+r put the state
socket in layer=resize; five bare h took the focused window 640 -> 615 (5px
each); one bare Right took it 615 -> 625 (10px — the coarse/fine split
survived); Escape returned the socket to default.

SIDE EFFECT: test-hotkeyd.sh stage 10 derives a still-i3-owned chord to seed a
duplicate with and matched single-segment chords only; $mod+r was the last one,
so the seed came up empty and the stage failed. Pattern widened to allow '+'
inside the chord.

title: Apps + session group cutover: $mod+9, $mod+Ctrl+m, $mod+F5, $mod+Shift+e leave i3
design:
The four remaining chords that are plain spawns — no modes, no layers, no i3 state:

  bindsym $mod+9 exec --no-startup-id blurlock                     (config.common:457)
  bindsym $mod+Ctrl+m exec terminal -e 'alsamixer'                 (config.common:65)
  bindsym $mod+F5 exec terminal -e 'mocp'                          (config.common:79)
  bindsym $mod+Shift+e exec "i3-nagbar -t warning -m '...' -b 'Yes, exit i3' 'i3-msg exit'"   (config.common:298)

NOT IN THIS GROUP, and each for a reason already written down:
- $mod+Shift+q (kill), $mod+Shift+c (reload), $mod+Shift+r (hammer),
  $mod+Ctrl+Shift+r (panic) — recovery keys. config.common:202 states the rule:
  a key whose job is to deal with something ALREADY misbehaving belongs in the
  engine that cannot lose its grabs. Grabs die with the daemon.
- $mod+Ctrl+t (picom), $mod+r (resize mode) — deletions to decide, not
  migrations (dotfiles-c57, dotfiles-9up; nav's Alt sublayer supersedes resize).
- $mod+Ctrl+x (xkill) — undecided: the recovery-key argument fits it but
  nothing says so. Settle separately, do not sweep it in here.
- $mod+Shift+o (i3-input rename) — nested quotes + pinned by
  test-notif-history PHASE 3; its own task.

TWO THINGS MEASURED BEFORE WRITING THIS, because both would fail silently:
1. PATH. Run actions execute with shell=True from the DAEMON's environment,
   not i3's. Checked /proc/<daemon>/environ: PATH carries /sbin, and terminal,
   blurlock, alsamixer, i3-nagbar all resolve there. No absolute-path rewrite
   needed (unlike the entry-point group, which uses ~/.local/bin/... paths).
2. mocp IS NOT INSTALLED on this host — $mod+F5 is already a dead bind in i3
   today. Migrate it VERBATIM anyway (a cutover moves behaviour, it does not
   silently curate it) and file the deadness separately.

SEMANTIC OVERLAP worth noting, not resolving here: the system layer already has
'e' -> i3exit logout, and $mod+Shift+e is exit-i3-with-a-nagbar. Two ways to
end the session. Migrating changes neither; whether one should go is a product
question for the retro.
acceptance_criteria:
1. binds.py carries all four; config.common carries none (comment pointers per the established convention).
2. zz-fallback-binds.conf gains all four verbatim, pinned by test_the_fallback_is_exactly_what_binds_py_owns_and_i3_does_not under Mod4 AND Mod1.
3. config-xrdp restates them if the proot session should keep them — same decision as dotfiles-hwds.43. State the choice explicitly either way.
4. FakeXServer stub keymap gains 9, F5, m, e (standard PC layout codes) — without them the chords resolve to keycode 0 and read as grab failures in unrelated tests.
5. Grab count rises by 4 on both displays; zero BadAccess.
6. pytest, test-hotkeyd.sh, test-panic.sh, test-nav-mode.sh, test-launcher.sh green; the two known-red-on-base suites (dotfiles-ph03, dotfiles-5quz) unchanged in count.
7. i3 -C clean on both entry points, normal and panic-linked trees.
8. LIVE on :10 (i3-msg reload THEN daemon restart): $mod+Ctrl+m opens alsamixer in a terminal exactly once. $mod+9 and $mod+Shift+e are NOT to be fired on the live session — one locks the screen, the other offers to end it; prove them by grab registration + a dispatch probe that substitutes a harmless command, never by pressing them for real.
close_reason:
DONE, commit c85c882. Self-verified (implementer == reviewer this session).

RED FIRST, both steps, under BOTH $mod resolutions:
- binds added while i3 still had them -> test_no_chord_is_owned_by_both_i3_and_
  the_daemon failed naming the four chords.
- removed from i3 before the fallback -> test_the_fallback_is_exactly_what_
  binds_py_owns_and_i3_does_not failed.

CRITERIA:
1/2. binds.py has all four, config.common none (comment pointers), fallback has
     all four verbatim; the exact-set test passes under Mod4 and Mod1.
3.   PROOT DECISION: not restated in config-xrdp, and the rule is now written
     down — restate what the platform model calls Core UX (the $mod+n / $mod+v
     pickers were), not host-specific desktop utilities. blurlock/alsamixer/mocp
     are the latter.
4.   Stub keymap gains 9/m/F5 (18/58/71).
5.   67 -> 71 grabs on BOTH displays, no BadAccess.
6.   pytest 399/0, test-hotkeyd.sh 132/0, test-panic.sh 54/0, test-launcher.sh
     27/0, test-nav-mode.sh both shapes. test-notif-history.sh 127/1 =
     dotfiles-ph03, red on base, count unchanged.
7.   i3 -C clean on i3/config and i3/config-xrdp.
8.   LIVE on :10 (reload THEN restart): $mod+Ctrl+m mapped exactly one
     'alsamixer' URxvt window; $mod+Shift+e mapped the nagbar (safe — exiting
     needs a click) and it was killed after. $mod+9 deliberately NOT fired on a
     live session: it locks the screen. That one rests on the grab count, the
     table validation and i3 no longer owning it — stated rather than dressed
     up as a live pass.

SIDE EFFECT WORTH REVIEW: the parser-floor assertion in test_binds.py was
repointed a third time (81->77, 77->51, now 12->8 tripped it). Changed from a
total-relative floor to the recovery set (>= 4), which cannot erode as the
migration finishes. Reviewer should sanity-check that reasoning rather than the
number.

DISCOVERED: dotfiles-hwds.47 (P4) -- $mod+F5 binds mocp, which is not installed.

title: hotkeyd.sh status proves LIVENESS not SERVING - a daemon with half its grabs lost still reports running
design:
Split out of dotfiles-hwds.41 (fixed in e0df62a2). During that outage the :10
daemon had lost the whole directional group and `hotkeyd.sh status` still
printed "running on :10 (pid ..., socket ...)". Liveness was true; serving was
not, and nothing in the tool could tell the difference.

The check that was missing: does the grab set match what the table asks for.
The daemon now keeps that wanted list (GrabManager._wanted), so the cheapest
form is to publish grabbed-count + wanted-count on the state socket and have
status compare them, reporting DEGRADED with the missing chords named.

Same family as dotfiles-hwds.28 (daemon survives its X server's death, status
lies) and dotfiles-hwds.29 (heartbeat absence indistinguishable from
staleness). Consider fixing the three together — each is "the tool answers a
weaker question than the user is asking".

Worth having regardless of hwds.41: a grab can still be legitimately refused
(i3 mid-restart, a stuck exclusive grab per dotfiles-hwds.30), and the user's
only current signal is a bind quietly not working.
close_reason:
DONE, commit fe3840ba. Self-verified.

RED FIRST: 6 of the 7 new tests failed before the implementation (grab_report,
the health code/message, ordering, tolerance of a missing report).

WHAT SHIPS: GrabManager.grab_report() (wanted/active/missing, missing NAMED, and
same-grab aliases like Tab/ISO_Left_Tab excluded rather than counted lost);
published to a SIDECAR file on every grab-set computation — not the lock file,
whose mtime is the heartbeat, or a re-grab would beat the heart for a wedged
daemon; health() probe 4 with new exit code 9; hotkeyd.sh relays 9.

ORDERING is deliberate and tested: a stale heartbeat, an unreachable display and
a foreign grab (dotfiles-hwds.30) each EXPLAIN missing grabs, so each is
reported INSTEAD of degradation. ABSENCE IS NOT DAMAGE — a pre-upgrade daemon
publishes no report and stays OK, which is dotfiles-hwds.29's mistake avoided.

Exit 9 vs 8 matters: 8 (foreign grab) cannot be fixed by restarting and says so;
9 IS fixed by a restart, because re-resolving the wanted set against the current
keymap is what start does.

STAGE 15 drives it end to end on real Xvfb. Note the mechanism: a typo cannot
produce this state — --check refuses an unknown keysym before startup — so the
stage reproduces the REAL cause, a keymap changing under a running daemon
(routine on :10 via xrdp reconnects), by deleting F11's keysyms with a real
ChangeKeyboardMapping and letting the real MappingNotify land. Control case
first so 'detects damage' is distinguishable from 'always complains'.

MUTATION: making health ignore the report reproduces the original signature
verbatim — 'hotkeyd: running on :42 (pid …, socket …)' with a chord confirmed
lost — and turns stage 15 red.

pytest 412/0, test-hotkeyd.sh 149/0, launcher 27/0, panic 54/0, nav both shapes.
LIVE :10: publishes {wanted:72, active:72, missing:[]}; --health reports
'serving (…, 72 chords grabbed)'.

REMAINING IN THE FAMILY: dotfiles-hwds.29 (heartbeat absence vs staleness) is
the last of the three 'the tool answers a weaker question than the user asked'
tickets; .28 and this one are now closed.

title: sp020: verify the $mod+Shift+<digit> workspace row from a REAL RDP client on :10, not XTEST
description: The workspace cutover (dotfiles-hwds.34) verified all three verbs live on :10, but by xdotool/XTEST injection. XTEST synthesises a clean Shift; xrdp wraps every character a real client sends in a synthetic Shift, which is the whole reason the nav layer uses Ctrl and not Shift as its move modifier (sp020). Passive grabs match on (keycode, mask) and i3 served this same row on :10 before the cutover, so parity is expected — but expected is not measured, and sp020 lists 'source-device / synthetic-Shift behaviour needs a human at an RDP client' as a known limitation. Press $mod+Shift+<n> from the Android RDP client on :10 and confirm the container moves and follows exactly once (a double-fire would move it, then move it again from wherever it landed).
notes:
MEASURED AND CLEAN, 2026-07-28, on the live xrdp :10 session with a real RDP client.

METHOD: ws-switch.nu 2 follow is IDEMPOTENT -- running it twice looks identical to running it once, so the visible result proves nothing. Probed for distinct PIDs of real ws-switch.nu runs instead (ps filtered on comm=nu AND args containing the script path, polled at 10ms). A nushell start lives ~100ms+, so two spawns even 5ms apart land in the same ps snapshot as two distinct PIDs.

PROBE VALIDATED BEFORE USE: 0 entries over 3s idle; 1 injected press -> 1 PID; 2 injected presses -> 2 PIDs. (First attempt matched 'pgrep -f ws-switch.nu' and logged 300 phantom fires by matching its OWN command line -- the fix is matching comm, not just args.)

RESULT: 6 real $mod+Shift+2 presses from the RDP client produced 6 distinct PIDs. Timestamps 20:07:25.8, 20:07:34.2, 20:08:07.4, 20:08:09.3, 20:08:11.5, 20:08:13.9 -- tightest gap 1.88s. A double-fire from xrdp's release-press-release delivery (dotfiles-hwds.24) would show two spawns tens of MILLISECONDS apart within one keystroke. Nothing of the kind.

CONCLUSION: xrdp's synthetic Shift does not disturb a passive grab on $mod+Shift+<character>. Expected, since a passive grab matches (keycode, mask) and i3 served this same row on :10 for years -- but now measured rather than argued. This unblocked the 8 $mod+Shift+<letter> move chords in the directional group (dotfiles-hwds.37).

SCOPE OF THE CLAIM: press path only. dotfiles-hwds.24 (on_release binds may double-fire on :10) is untouched by this -- the daemon's table has had no on_release bind since $mod+Shift+d was dropped.
close_reason: Closed

title: State socket replays nothing until the first layer change, so a healthy daemon looks wedged
design:
Found while diagnosing dotfiles-hwds.28. Not fixed there because the fix
collides with an intentional guard and needs a decision rather than a patch.

StatePublisher._current stays None until LayerEngine._publish fires, and
_publish is change-only. So between daemon startup and the first layer change,
a client that connects is accepted and sent NOTHING (layers.py:558 —
`if self._current is not None:`).

TWO CONSEQUENCES:

1. IT MISLEADS DIAGNOSIS. This is literally what the hwds.28 report cited as
   evidence of a zombie: "socket accepts connections but never replays state
   (2s+ timeout)". It is what a perfectly healthy, freshly started daemon does.
   An operator probing the state socket to decide whether a daemon is serving
   gets silence from a healthy one, which is the same answer a wedged one gives.
   (hwds.28 worked around this by heartbeating the lock file instead, so the
   launcher no longer depends on the socket — but anything else that probes the
   socket still hits this.)

2. IT IS A USER-VISIBLE BAR BUG. ft009's whole point is replay-on-connect: "a
   bar that starts late must never be blank, which the i3-binding-event feed
   could not manage" (layers.py:559-561). A bar that starts before the first nav
   of the session gets exactly the blank it was promised it would not.

THE OBVIOUS FIX AND WHY IT IS NOT OBVIOUS. Prime _current with the engine's
seeded starting state ({"layer": "default", "mod": null}) so replay-on-connect
always answers. That collides with
test_a_freshly_started_daemon_replays_nothing_to_a_client in test_daemon.py,
which is a deliberate dotfiles-hwds.27 "cause 2" guard: a daemon must not serve
a layer it computed before reading real modifier state.

The two are arguably not in conflict — the seeded state is `default`/null, which
is not an invented layer, and LayerEngine._last_published is already seeded with
exactly it — but that is a judgement about what hwds.27's guard was protecting,
and it changes what every bar receives on connect. Decide before patching, and
if the answer is "prime it", rewrite the hwds.27 guard to assert the narrower
property it actually means (no NON-DEFAULT layer before real input) rather than
deleting it.
close_reason: RESOLVED by sp021 Go rewrite (audited during dotfiles-ylmp.17). hotkeyd/internal/layer/publisher.go:3-25 doc comment names dotfiles-4uiu explicitly: NewStatePublisher(path string, initial State) (publisher.go:183) requires the engine's actual starting state as a constructor argument (wired from Engine.State(), always valid immediately after NewEngine per the doc comment) -- there is no nil/absent _current to fall through as Python's StatePublisher had, so accept-time replay always answers. Structural fix, not a patch.

title: test-panic.sh header claims the shipped fallback binds nothing; it now binds the whole nav mode

title: test-nav-mode.sh runs only the :0 shape — sp020 T14 requires the :10 ($mod=Mod1) shape too
design:
sp020 Task 14's test_plan: 'every behaviour case runs on an :10-shaped display with $mod = Mod1, and the suite asserts zero BadAccess plus a clean check --ownership before any behaviour assertion is believed. A green behaviour run on a display where the daemon holds no grabs is the exact false pass being designed out.'

dotfiles-8qju delivered the re-point plus BOTH ownership assertions (zero BadAccess at startup and after all three sublayers; no nav bind left in i3's loaded config) -- but only on the :0 shape. i3/test-nav-mode.sh:~90 hardcodes 'set $mod Mod4' in its harness.conf.

WHY THE MISSING SHAPE IS THE INTERESTING ONE. On :10 $mod is Mod1, so nav's RESIZE chords (Alt+hjkl) ARE i3's global $mod+hjkl focus binds. That collision is what reverted T6 (fd9e9f2): the daemon took BadAccess on all eight and Alt+h fell through to i3 as a focus. config.common:381-388 claims the XI2 port resolves it and cites a measurement (width 512 -> 461) -- but that measurement is a one-off note in a comment, not an assertion any suite re-runs.

WHAT TO DO: parameterise the harness over $mod -- 'set $mod $NAV_TEST_MOD' in harness.conf plus the matching X resource (i3wm.mod) so the daemon resolves the same value, per sp020's 'daemon $mod must equal i3's $mod while i3 still owns binds in the same group' convention -- and run the whole file twice. The zero-BadAccess assertion already exists and is where the Mod1 run pays off: it is the assertion whose absence let the reverted cutover merge green.

Not done in 8qju because that task's scope was 're-point the suite at the daemon', and doubling the matrix is a second, larger change.
close_reason:
Suite now runs both shapes; Mod1 (:10 xrdp) added and mutation-verified. Commit 07c1fef5.

Found three defects while building it, each of which made the new run pass while proving nothing -- the first version reported 40/40 on Mod1 while measuring the Mod4 daemon throughout:
1. xrdb -merge exits 0 and writes NOTHING against an Xvfb display (xrdb -query empty, xprop -root RESOURCE_MANAGER 'not found', with or without -nocpp). Replaced with a python-xlib property write.
2. An X server RESETS when its last client disconnects, discarding root-window properties. The resource was written by a short-lived process that was the only client, so it was wiped as it landed. Xvfb now runs -noreset. Real sessions never see this because i3 holds a connection throughout.
3. The injected chord was hardcoded 'xdotool key super+o' in all four sites, so parameterising the config side alone left the Mod1 run pressing Super. Now derived from the shape.

Guard on the guard: the harness reads the resource back through hotkeyd.x_resource_mod and aborts on mismatch before any assertion runs.

Mutation-verified: dropping the resource write -> FATAL shape mismatch; pressing super+o on the Mod1 run -> 6 failures led by 'the daemon publishes layer=nav'. Both shapes 40/0.

title: i3/test-events.py is dead code after the nav suite's daemon re-point
design:
dotfiles-8qju re-pointed i3/test-nav-mode.sh at hotkeyd's state socket. Its only two consumers of i3/test-events.py -- the 'nop nav-move-on|nop nav-move-off' and 'nop nav-resize-on|nop nav-resize-off' scenarios -- are gone, because i3 has no nav binds left to emit binding events for. close_reason: WON'T FIX, deliberately. i3/test-events.py is dead as a test dependency after the nav suite's daemon re-pointing, but adr0015 cites it by path as a worked example of 'an X client with an event loop and no nushell fit' -- one of the four references that justify Python being an allowed language here. title: test_qs_focus_border_mode.py: 8 suppression assertions stale since the screenshot rework
design:
quickshell/test_qs_focus_border_mode.py fails 8 assertions on plain main (verified against git show main: copies of both the test and qs-focus-border.py, run in isolation). They all encode the OLD screenshot contract: 'screenshot mode enter hides border'. Commit 29106e6 (feat(screenshot): highlight focused window, hide ring on drag start) deliberately changed that — entering 'screenshot' now COLOURS the ring and suppression moved to the synthetic 'screenshot-drag' mode — but the suite was not updated with it.

Failing: mode-enter binding arms suppression (no redraw), screenshot mode enter hides border, mode-only entry (no binding) hides border, mode-only entry (no binding) still suppresses refresh, refresh while suppressed is a no-op, save path: still hidden after mode entry, save path: close noise during suppression does not redraw, overlay-never-started: border hidden at mode enter.

Pre-existing and unrelated to dotfiles-hwds.2/.9 (the layer-feed work added 16 assertions to this file, all passing). The suite is currently a permanent-red gate, so it cannot catch a real regression. Fix: re-point the 8 assertions at 'screenshot-drag' where suppression actually lives now.
close_reason:
FIXED, commit 795c5e12. Suite green (was 8 failures on plain main). Assertions were wrong, code was right — same shape as dotfiles-ph03.

29106e6 split the capture into two phases and moved suppression between them:
  'screenshot'      AIMING — ring stays UP and is RECOLOURED (COLOR_MODES)
  'screenshot-drag' DRAWING — ring HIDES, refreshes stay blocked (SUPPRESS_MODES)
The suite still encoded the pre-29106e6 'entering screenshot hides' contract for
both. Every suppression case re-pointed at screenshot-drag; the module docstring,
which stated the old contract as fact, rewritten to describe the split.

DID NOT JUST DELETE THE 8. That would have left nothing asserting what 29106e6
introduced. The aiming phase is now pinned positively (does NOT hide, DOES set
mode_colored, leaves refreshes working, colour clears on leave), plus the aim->
drag transition the user actually performs, which neither phase's own assertions
covered: it must end hidden AND suppressed though the mode it came from was
neither.

The binding-arm case is re-pointed and its branch documented as DEFENSIVE, not
dead: qs-region.py enters screenshot-drag by direct i3-msg, and $mod+Shift+s
left i3 with the screenshot group (dotfiles-hwds.39), so no binding event
reaches this flow at all today.

MUTATION, both reverted after:
- SUPPRESS_MODES back to {'screenshot','screenshot-drag'}: exactly the two
  aiming assertions go red, nothing else.
- COLOR_MODES emptied: 4 red — the new colour assertion plus the three existing
  colour-state ones, so the new case fails for its own reason.

git diff on qs-focus-border.py is empty; no production code touched. pytest
399/0 unchanged.

With dotfiles-ph03 also closed, no suite in the repo is red on base.

title: $mod+Shift+r: restart i3 AND cycle the daemon, so the daemon re-grabs after i3
design:
User's design call (2026-07-28): "$mod+Shift+r ... no fallback just restart
deamos too".

WHAT IS WANTED: $mod+Shift+r stays a RESET key -- it restarts i3 as it does
today, and additionally restarts the hotkeyd daemon. This is NOT panic. No
fallback table is linked, no latch is set, the daemon comes back.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND CONVENIENCE. This fixes the ownership flip measured during
dotfiles-hwds.13. i3 restart re-runs exec_always, which calls `hotkeyd.sh start`
-- but start refuses when a daemon already holds the display (hotkeyd.sh:95,
exit 3, "already running") and spawns nothing. So on an i3 restart:

  - i3 re-reads its config and re-grabs every chord it declares
  - the daemon does NOT re-grab (sync_binds only re-registers chords whose
    (code, mask) changed, so SIGHUP does not help either)
  - since core and XI2 passive grabs are in separate conflict domains and the
    LATER grabber wins (dotfiles-f224), i3 silently takes any contested chord
    and keeps it until the daemon is restarted by hand

Measured, real i3 + real daemon:
    fresh session          i3: default   daemon: nav     -> daemon owns
    after i3 restart       i3: nav       daemon: default -> i3 owns, permanently

Restarting the daemon as part of the same key restores the intended ownership,
because the daemon then grabs AFTER i3.

DESIGN -- the ordering does the work, no sleep or race:

    bindsym $mod+Shift+r exec --no-startup-id \
        ~/.dotfiles/hotkeyd/hotkeyd.sh stop; restart

  1. `hotkeyd.sh stop` on the caller's display -- grabs die with the process
  2. i3 `restart` -- re-execs i3, which re-grabs its own chords
  3. exec_always fires as part of that restart and calls `hotkeyd.sh start`,
     which now succeeds because step 1 cleared the daemon

Net effect: i3 grabs first, daemon grabs second, daemon wins its own chords --
which is the intended steady state. No sleep, no polling; exec_always already
runs at the right moment.

Verify the i3 command-chaining semantics before relying on the one-liner: i3
parses `exec ...; restart` as two commands, and `--no-startup-id` plus the
argument boundary need checking. If the chaining is ambiguous, use a tiny
wrapper script instead of fighting the parser.

SCOPE: caller's display only. i3 restart affects one i3, so only that display's
daemon needs cycling. Do NOT make this machine-wide -- that is panic's job and
panic deliberately owns the machine-wide behaviour (dotfiles-hwds.12
requirement 4).

DOES NOT CHANGE:
- $mod+Shift+F12 stays the panic bind, unchanged, with the fallback table and
  the sticky latch. Reset and panic are different tools: reset assumes the
  daemon is healthy and wants a clean cycle; panic assumes it is broken and
  hands the keyboard back to i3.
- PANIC_CHORD and the validator reservation stay on $mod+Shift+F12.

SEQUENCING: queued behind dotfiles-hwds.25 (single source of truth), which is
rewriting binds.py and config.common right now. After .25 lands, $mod+Shift+r
will be a single declaration in binds.py with owner=I3, so this becomes a
one-line change in one file -- the benefit .25 exists to deliver.

TESTS: assert the real effect, not the exit code. Start a daemon on a throwaway
display, confirm it owns a chord, fire the reset bind's exact command string,
then confirm the daemon is running again AND still owns the chord. A test that
only checks the daemon is alive would pass while the chord sat with i3.
Reuse hwds.12's GET_CONFIG-including-included_configs technique for ownership.
close_reason: Obsoleted by the panic-chord move (4ff96794): $mod+Shift+r is now the PANIC bind, because the Android RDP client has no F12 and the escape hatch had to be reachable. The underlying defect (i3 restart re-grabs, daemon does not, so i3 keeps a contested chord) is real but no longer bites -- after the nav cutover i3 and the daemon share no chord. Re-file if a future migration reintroduces one. Forced past the .25 dep: .25 is itself obsolete.

title: hotkeyd: run_daemon's loop wiring has zero unit coverage — a dropped pump_i3() ships green without Xvfb
design:
Found during the dotfiles-hwds.10 audit while re-running the implementer's mutation M3.

MUTANT M3: delete `dae.pump_i3()` from run_daemon's loop body (hotkeyd.py:855).
RESULT: pytest 232 passed, 0 failed — ZERO unit kills.
        test-hotkeyd.sh stage 11 — 6 FAIL, reproducing the original defect
        verbatim ('daemon published layer=nav while i3 holds a mode',
        'BadAccess during the refused entry: 7', 'two owners: i3=resize
        daemon=nav', 'published 0 default lines, want 1').

This is not 'uncovered' — run_daemon IS driven as a real process by stages 8, 11
and 12, and test-hotkeyd.sh:163 documents that split on purpose ('The run_daemon
zone had ZERO coverage in any style, which is exactly why the SIGHUP kill and the
skipped startup validation shipped').

The residual risk is the GATING, not the absence: every stage that exercises
run_daemon is behind `command -v Xvfb` / `command -v xdotool` and SKIPs when
they are missing. On such a box (CI container, fresh WSL, Termux) the whole
call-site wiring of run_daemon — pump_i3, the i3 fd in the select() wait set,
resync_grabs on transition, the reload path — can be deleted and the suite is
still green. The unit suite drives dae.pump_i3() directly, never the loop that
calls it.

DIRECTION (not prescriptive): a unit test that runs run_daemon's loop body against
the existing FakeXServer + FakeI3 for a bounded number of iterations (stop['flag']
after N, or a fake clock) would kill M3 in pytest. The pieces already exist —
test_daemon.py has FakeXServer, FakeI3 and Lines — what is missing is a seam that
lets the loop be stepped without a real Xlib display and a real select().

Alternatively, make the Xvfb-gated stages FAIL rather than SKIP when the suite is
run with an explicit --require-live flag, so the post-merge gate cannot pass on a
box that silently skipped every process-level assertion.
close_reason: RESOLVED by sp021 Go rewrite (audited during dotfiles-ylmp.17). hotkeyd/cmd/hotkeyd/daemon_test.go:591-593 explicitly names 'the exact dotfiles-eez2 mutant (M3: delete dae.pump_i3() from the loop body)'. TestRun_EventBranch_PumpsI3, TestRun_TimeoutBranch_PumpsI3, TestRun_PumpI3_Reconnect_ResyncsI3Mode, TestRun_PumpI3_PollEventsError_LoggedAndLoopContinues exercise the run loop's i3-pump wiring as ordinary Go unit tests -- verified passing: 'go test ./cmd/hotkeyd/... -run TestRun_.*PumpsI3|...' all PASS, no Xvfb/xdotool gate required. Closes the exact coverage gap eez2 reported.

title: test-hotkeyd.sh:201 reads the caller's real panic latch (status exit 4)
design:
Found during the dotfiles-hwds.21 audit. Sibling of dotfiles-f2be (same class:
a hotkeyd suite reading machine-wide state it does not own). Currently INERT —
no fallback link exists in the real ~/.i3/config.d today.

hwds.21 made `hotkeyd.sh status` read the panic latch on the DAEMON-RUNNING
branch (hotkeyd.sh:176 -> exit 4). Every suite that drives the launcher
sandboxes that read except one:

  test-launcher.sh:23   export HOTKEYD_I3_CONFIG_D="$RUNTIME/i3-config.d"  (throwaway, never populated)
  test-panic.sh:76,78   export HOME="$T/home"; HOTKEYD_I3_CONFIG_D="$HOME/.i3/config.d"
  test-hotkeyd.sh:201   NEITHER — reads the caller's real $HOME/.i3/config.d

test-hotkeyd.sh:201 is:

    if DISPLAY=$D8 XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$T8" "$HERE/hotkeyd.sh" status >/dev/null 2>&1
    then ok "launcher finds a daemon started with extra flags"
    else bad "launcher's pgrep pattern misses a flag-carrying daemon"

It hand-starts a daemon on $D8 and uses status's exit code as a proxy for "the
pgrep pattern matched". Before hwds.21 that path returned 0 regardless of the
latch. After hwds.21, if the OPERATOR'S OWN session is panicked while the suite
runs, status returns 4 and the assertion reports "launcher's pgrep pattern
misses a flag-carrying daemon" — a misleading diagnostic naming the wrong
subsystem, during an outage. That is the exact failure class hwds.19/.20/.21
exist to eliminate.

Note the relevant transition is 0 -> 4, not 1 -> 4: the concern is not that 4
and 1 are conflated (they are, harmlessly) but that a previously-passing path
now fails on operator state the suite does not control.

Reachability is narrow but not theoretical: autostart is armed on both displays
(a76e9a9), panic is one chord away ($mod+Shift+F12), and running the hotkeyd
suites straight after a panic is the obvious debugging move.

FIX: sandbox the read the way the other two suites already do — export
HOTKEYD_I3_CONFIG_D to a throwaway dir in test-hotkeyd.sh, or scope it to the
stage-8 block around line 201. One line. Optionally assert the exit code is 0
specifically rather than merely zero, so the assertion says what it means.

Not a defect in shipped behaviour — hotkeyd.sh's contract is correct. This is
test hermeticity only.
close_reason: Fixed directly, see commit. pytest 322, test-hotkeyd.sh 107/0, i3 -C clean.

title: test-panic.sh is not hermetic against a second checkout running the same suite
design:
Found while implementing dotfiles-hwds.20/.21 (two agents running hotkeyd suites in parallel worktrees).

hotkeyd-panic.sh's target_displays() pgreps EVERY hotkeyd.py on the box. That is
CORRECT production behaviour — panic is machine-wide by the Task 10 decision and
must not miss a daemon — but it makes test-panic.sh non-hermetic: a daemon
belonging to another checkout of this repo lands in the suite's throwaway
$STATE, panic stops it, and resume then tries to restart it under the suite's
fake HOME and fails.

REPRODUCED. A run whose displays were :81/:82 attempted a start on :87 (a
sibling agent's display) and resume exited 1:

    hotkeyd.sh: failed to start — see /tmp/tmp.xPKeQhbdeo/home/.local/state/hotkeyd-87.log
    hotkeyd-panic.sh: the daemon did not come back on every display

Measured flake rate while a sibling suite was live: ~1 in 3 runs, in sections
1, 6 and 8. Zero failures in 8 consecutive runs once the sibling went idle, and
zero under a deliberately hostile always-alive foreign daemon after hwds.20
stopped asserting resume's rc in its own case.

STILL EXPOSED: section 6 asserts resume's exit code directly
('[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || bad "resume exited $rc"'). It survives a foreign daemon
that stays up (the launcher returns 3, which resume treats as success) but fails
for one that is alive at panic and gone by resume. Section 8's daemon-count
assertions have the same shape and tolerate it only by not reading rc.

FIX OPTIONS (do NOT narrow target_displays in production — a panic that misses a
daemon fails AWAY from the latch, which is the direction that must never break):
- run the suite under its own PID/mount namespace, or
- have the suite refuse to start when a foreign hotkeyd.py is already alive
  (fail fast with a named skip rather than a confusing mid-suite failure), or
- accept and document it, and serialise hotkeyd suites across agents.

Cheap first step: the fail-fast skip. It converts a misleading 'resume exited 1'
into 'another hotkeyd daemon is running on this machine — skipped'.

title: live_check auto-repeat assert may pass vacuously — Xvfb delivers no repeat stream
design:
Found incidentally during dotfiles-hwds.4 (coalescer-fairness tests), reported
but deliberately not fixed there -- closing it is production-adjacent and wants
its own task.

CLAIM UNDER SUSPICION: live_check.py's existing check "a held key fires ONCE
despite the real auto-repeat stream" (the G3 case from T4). It holds a grabbed
key for 1.2s via XTEST and asserts exactly 1 dispatch.

FINDING: a standalone probe measured a 0.6s XTEST hold of a grabbed key
delivering NO auto-repeat events at all under the suite's Xvfb. If repeat never
materialises, the assert "exactly 1 dispatch" is satisfied trivially -- it would
pass against a daemon with no coalescing whatsoever, which is the coverage-gaming
shape the suite exists to avoid.

NOT CONCLUSIVE: the hwds.4 N4 mutant DID fail that same check on one run, so
repeat does sometimes materialise. So the check is flaky-vacuous rather than
always-vacuous, which is worse than either -- it passes for the wrong reason most
of the time and occasionally for the right one.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Determine whether Xvfb honours XTEST-driven auto-repeat at all, and under what
   settings (xset r rate / XkbSetAutoRepeatRate on the test display).
2. Either make repeat deterministic on the test display, or add a PRECONDITION
   assert that fails loudly when no repeat stream was observed -- the pattern
   hwds.4 used for its fairness checks, where a precondition read off the same
   run proves the judged phenomenon actually occurred.
3. A vacuous-pass guard belongs on every live timing check, not just this one.

WHY IT MATTERS: auto-repeat coalescing is what stops a held nav key firing 30
times. If the only test of it is trivially satisfiable, the guard is unprotected
and a refactor can silently remove it -- exactly how the coalescer guards in
hwds.4 came to be mutation-proven-unconstrained in the first place.
close_reason:
FIXED, commit above. Self-verified.

PREMISE DID NOT REPRODUCE: measured under the suite's Xvfb, the 1.2s XTEST hold
delivers 15 presses / 14 flagged / 1 release — a real repeat stream. The ticket
predates the XI2 port, which changed the mechanism (XIKeyRepeat on the press,
no synthetic release) and added the counts-read-off-this-run check.

THE REAL HOLE WAS STRUCTURAL: precondition and claim were two INDEPENDENT
checks, so a repeat-less run printed FAIL + PASS, and that PASS was a green line
for an untested claim (1 dispatch from 1 press is free). Now coupled via a new
judged() helper — no phenomenon, no pass; a repeat-less run reports CANNOT JUDGE
with the observed counts inline.

MUTATION: forcing the precondition false turns the claim PASS -> 'FAIL … CANNOT
JUDGE — no repeat stream this run, so 1 dispatch would be free'. Pre-commit, the
same mutant left it green.

Ticket item 3 (the guard belongs on every live timing check): the fairness
checks below already carry preconditions read off their own run — that pattern
came from dotfiles-hwds.4 — so this was the one claim standing without one.
judged() is the shared shape for future ones.
